title: Empyrean / Aether Bus Protocol (Phase 1 thin slice)
description: Source-of-truth message schema for the Aether bus (the Empyrean suite's shared protocol). PARTIAL, and precisely so as of 2026-08-15 (protocol.md §11.5/§11.6): the envelope, the handshake, every event, the symbol primitive, and a growing subset of §6's catalogued methods are schematized here. THE COUNT IS DELIBERATELY NOT STATED IN THIS PROSE (2026-08-22): it was hand-maintained across six recounts and was STILL wrong, this sentence reading '37' while the file held 58, which is the very defect its own later clause names, that a count carried forward is a count nobody checked. Repairing the number would only reset that clock, so the number is gone instead. The gate at schema/tests/validate_contract_schema.py derives every count BY PARSING this file and prints them on each run; that output is the only authority, and the BLOCKED rows print there too. Every fragment is written FROM ITS §6 ROW and none from a server's replies, which is §8's required direction) — which covers every method the reference server advertises, both params and result, plus the rows schematized AHEAD OF BEING SERVED, because §8 item 20 makes the fragment the precondition for the handler and not its record: emulator/read_cram and emulator/write_cram (the CRAM pair), and since 2026-08-26 the whole BREAKPOINT family, whose four fragments were rewritten to §11.21 (CR-BP) — handle-identified, with emulator/breakpoint_set_enabled added as the one writer of `enabled`. NO SERVER SERVES THAT SHAPE TODAY and that is the intended order: the successor serves capabilities.breakpoints false, the legacy server serves the pre-amendment ADDRESS-named rows and §11.21 freezes rather than migrates it, so this file describes the surface a server implements against rather than one it has already shipped. FIVE §6 ROWS REMAIN UNSCHEMATIZED AND DELIBERATELY SO — z80_registers, read_vdp_registers, read_vsram, call_stack, log_tail — because each states its result too loosely to transcribe without inventing (a literal `…` in a key set, an array with no item type, or, for log_tail, a question §10 leaves openly undecided). The set was EIGHT until 2026-08-26, when object_slot, object_list and player_state left it under §11.25: they are schematized as a CLOSED ENVELOPE over a typed-open `fields` payload with a REQUIRED `layout` discriminant, which is the audit's own D-27 unblock condition and the reason the partial-fragment objection does not reach them — a typed-open map declares its incompleteness as a type, where a partial fragment asserts a completeness it does not have. That objection stands undiminished for the five above: a PARTIAL fragment would be worse than none, because item 20's closure would then refuse the conformant server that emits the keys the fragment omitted, while §2.5 already reads an ABSENT fragment correctly as 'not yet transcribed'. Each remaining row is itemized, with what would unblock it, in docs/2026-08-22-protocol-schema-audit.md, and the gate at schema/tests/validate_contract_schema.py DERIVES the blocked set by diffing §6 against `methods` and prints it on every run so none goes quiet — that output is the authority for the count, exactly as it is for the fragment count, and this prose is not. The authoritative live method set is whatever `initialize` advertises. REQUEST PARAMS ARE CLOSED HERE (protocol.md §2.5, §8 item 22, added 2026-08-19 by §11.17): every methods.<name>.params object declares `unevaluatedProperties: false`, and unlike item 20's RESULT closure — which is deliberately kept out of this file, so a stale copy cannot reject a conformant server — that keyword IS published, because on the request path the party validating is the party publishing what it supports. handshake.initialize.params is deliberately exempt: closing the handshake would make a version-skewed negotiation fail at the one step whose job is to survive it. PRECEDENCE (protocol.md D14): this file is NORMATIVE for wire shapes — which keys exist, their JSON types and ranges, whether they are required — while protocol.md is normative for semantics and behaviour. A disagreement between the two is a spec bug to be fixed by amendment in the pass that finds it; until amended, this file governs what goes on the wire. It is not a place to introduce behaviour: a shape here with no counterpart in protocol.md is an un-specced field, and §8's ban on unilateral invention applies. The two are amended together.

hex.description: Address or byte blob as a hex string (D9 category 1).

symbolName.description: A symbol's IDENTIFYING spelling, exactly as the listing writes it (protocol.md §4). It MUST round-trip: passing it back as lookup_symbol's `name`, or as any method's `symbol` param, MUST resolve to the same symbol — which is D7 made operable. The pattern forbids exactly one thing: a trailing `+$<hex>` displacement suffix. A displacement belongs in the reply's OWN numeric field (`disp`, `symbolDisp`), and a name carrying it duplicates a number the same reply already holds, inside a string a client would have to parse to get it back — §2.4's 'MUST NOT parse' and the same defect §11.5 struck run_to.stoppedAtFrame for. Mangling is NOT forbidden: `$engine.boot$EntryPoint$wait_dma` is a legitimate identifying name and the pattern accepts it, because `$` is only rejected in the `+$hex`-at-the-end position. Expressed as a pattern rather than as a sentence for D14's stated reason — a schema either accepts a message or does not.

hash64.description: A 64-bit FNV-1a fingerprint, spelled as a hex string of exactly 16 digits (protocol.md §6's '16-hex FNV-1a each', read through D9 category 1 — a hex value on this bus is a hex string). A fingerprint is compared, never computed on, so the fixed width is part of the type: a 15-digit answer is a leading zero somebody dropped, and two servers that disagree about padding produce fingerprints that never match.

hash32.description: A CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3 / zlib polynomial) fingerprint, spelled as a hex string of exactly 8 digits (D9 category 1). Fixed width for hash64's reason: a fingerprint is compared, never computed on, and a 7-digit answer is a dropped leading zero.

handle.description: An opaque handle (D9 category 4): a value the server issues purely so the client can hand it back — a checkpoint `id`, a list `cursor`. A string, deliberately: a client MUST NOT parse, order, compare or do arithmetic on one, and a number would invite exactly that. The representation is the server's business (protocol.md §6.1).

items.description: This page of the list. Item shape is the owning method's business; the envelope around it is not.

total.description: How many items exist, not how many were returned.

returned.description: items.length, restated so a client can compare it to `total` without counting.

truncated.description: REQUIRED EVEN WHEN FALSE (protocol.md §2.4 clause (a)): absence and `false` must not both mean 'you have everything', for the same reason droppedEvents is always present (§2.3).

cursor.description: Continuation handle. Present ONLY on methods that accept a cursor param — §2.4 clause (b): a method that accepts no continuation MUST NOT emit one, because a token that can never be handed back trains clients that handles are ignorable and publishes the server's position for nothing (D9 category 4's opacity argument). Behaviour is normative (§2.4 clause (c)); representation is the server's.

limit.description: The page ceiling the server actually applied, which is not necessarily the one the client asked for.

boundedList.description: The container for a list that is a FIELD of a result (protocol.md §2.4). A list that IS the whole result keeps the flat spelling its §6 row gives it — the array under its own name with total/returned/limit/truncated/cursor? as siblings — which is emulator/checkpoint_list. Identical field set, identical rules; only the nesting differs. Governs POLICY-bounded lists (a bound the server chose). A STRUCTURALLY bounded list — emulator/pixel_attribution's `candidates`, capped at 4 by the video hardware — takes neither the flag nor the cursor, because a list that cannot be partial has no partial-list failure mode (§2.4 clause (d)).

running.description: Whether the machine was free-running when this payload was built.

stamp.description: The machine stamp (protocol.md §2.2, D11). Present on every result, every error.data, and every event's params. Emulated clocks only — never wall-clock. Applied envelope-level after the handler returns, overwriting any same-named key. What a `frame` IS — the basis these clocks are expressed in — is advertised once in the initialize result as `timingBasis` (D16).

droppedEvents.description: Server→client events discarded on THIS connection since it opened (protocol.md §2.3, D17). Monotonically non-decreasing, cumulative, and always present — 0 is the answer, not the absence of one. Not part of the stamp (the stamp is a machine coordinate every connection sees identically; this is a per-connection fact) and never present on an event.

replyFields.description: The full envelope field set carried by every SUCCESS result and every error.data: the machine stamp (§2.2) plus the dropped-event counter (§2.3). Events carry `stamp` only.

method.$comment: Role-namespaced, snake_case, digits allowed after the first character (D3). The digits matter: the previous pattern `^([a-z]+/)?[a-z_]+$` rejected three catalogued methods — emulator/z80_read, emulator/z80_write, emulator/z80_registers — and nothing caught it because nothing validated against this file. Fixed 2026-08-15 (protocol.md §11.2); checked against every method name in protocol.md §6. Request methods only: EVENT names are camelCase (emulator/romReloaded, §3) and are matched by #/$defs/notification, which deliberately carries no pattern.

id.$comment: NULL IS PERMITTED HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE (CR-15, protocol.md §11.4). JSON-RPC 2.0 §5: 'If there was an error in detecting the id in the Request Object (e.g. Parse error/Invalid Request), it MUST be Null.' protocol.md §2 adopts JSON-RPC 2.0 wholesale and §8 item 2 makes it a conformance item, so the adopted standard MANDATED a value this schema excluded — a server answering a -32700 or a -32600 had no conformant option at all. Deliberately NOT widened in #/$defs/id: a request must carry a real id (an id-less request is a notification, matched by #/$defs/notification), and a success response echoes the request's id, so null is meaningless in both. The `allOf` below narrows it further, to the two codes that mandate it.

allOf.$comment: A null id is permitted ONLY on the two codes decided before a request object exists: -32700 (parse error) and -32600 (invalid request). Every other code answers a request the server DID parse, so a real id was available to echo and a null one is a correlation bug — the client cannot match the failure to the call that caused it, which is the silent-wrong-answer class this contract exists to prevent (D11's argument, applied to the error path). Expressed as if/then rather than in prose alone so it is mechanically enforced, per D14's reason for making the schema the tiebreaker at all.

code.description: -32700 parse | -32600 invalid request | -32601 method not found | -32602 invalid params | -32603 internal | -32000 not wired | -32004 addr out of range | -32005 invalid state for this operation | -32010 timeout | -32012 no symbols | -32013 symbol not found | -32015 unsupported protocol version

reason.description: Machine-readable discriminant. REQUIRED for -32005, e.g. machineRunning | checkpointCapReached | unknownCheckpoint | watchCapReached | breakpointCapReached | unknownBreakpoint | objectPoolFull | unknownSlot | slotOwnedByEntityWindow | mailboxNotConsumed | frameMoved | mailboxLayoutUnexpected (protocol.md §5). NOT AN ENUM, deliberately, for §11.18's reason — an emitted enum is unwidenable, and this registry grows by amendment. breakpointCapReached and unknownBreakpoint were added 2026-08-26 by §11.21: `breakpointCapReached` carries `cap` and `count` as integers beside it — the shape watchCapReached and checkpointCapReached already use, since a cap refusal that does not say what the cap was makes the client discover it by being refused twice — and `unknownBreakpoint` carries no further context, being the answer to a handle the server does not hold (emulator/breakpoint_set_enabled refuses; emulator/breakpoint_clear does not, and succeeds with removed 0). The LAST SIX were added 2026-09-03 by §11.32 (CR-J) and belong to the three object MUTATION rows, whose whole point is that a refusal by the game reaches the client as an error and never as a result field (§8 item 25): `objectPoolFull` (nothing was evicted, and the message must say so, because a client's next instinct is to retry harder; `data` carries the dynamic pool's size where layout resolves it), `unknownSlot` (the unknownCheckpoint/unknownBreakpoint precedent verbatim, covering three realities the engine cannot distinguish — the slot died, the handle was never a dynamic slot, the handle is malformed — with `handle` in `data`), `slotOwnedByEntityWindow` (refused for coherence, not malformedness; the message must name the fix, since the slot despawns on its own and MOVE is allowed on it), `mailboxNotConsumed` (the commonest error a user will meet, because the consumer exists in exactly one game state, so its `message` MUST say that the game is not in a state that services this mailbox rather than leaving a reader to call the feature broken; carries `cancelled` and `framesAdvanced`), `frameMoved` (expectFrameToken did not match the current stamp) and `mailboxLayoutUnexpected` (the resolved cells were not contiguous in the published order with the flag highest; the resolved order rides in `data`).

cancelled.description: Added 2026-09-03 by §11.32 (CR-J, Q2). On -32005 mailboxNotConsumed: the server cleared the request flag, so the request the client made can no longer fire. TRUE is the answer this reason always carries, and it is declared rather than left to prose because the alternative reading — an armed mailbox left behind after an error reply — is a world-change traced to a failure, and a client must be able to tell the two apart mechanically. error.data is an OPEN shape (it composes replyFields and closes nothing), so declaring the key adds its TYPE rather than its permission; cap and count, the same per-reason kind of key, remain prose-only in `reason` above, which is a pre-existing asymmetry this entry did not create.

framesAdvanced.description: Added 2026-09-03 by §11.32 (CR-J). The object mutation rows MUST report framesAdvanced on every reply, SUCCESS AND FAILURE (protocol.md §6 rule (5)), and the failure half of that obligation lands here: a caller whose request was refused after the machine advanced must still be able to say where the machine ended up. Same field, same meaning and same typing as the success-path key on emulator/object_spawn / _move / _delete.

data.description: Always present: it carries the machine stamp (D11) and droppedEvents (D17), plus any structured context.

watchStamp.description: A deterministic emulated coordinate for one matched access (protocol.md §6). The same shape a stop record uses, so a stop and a hit name the same kind of point. Never wall-clock. Nested rather than top-level: the envelope stamp (§2.2) overwrites same-named keys at the top level of a result.

engine.description: The server's name for the layout it decoded against. A FREE STRING, never an enum: §11.18 makes an emitted enum unwidenable, and this value's whole job is to grow one entry per supported game. Clients compare for equality; they do not switch on a closed set.

detectedBy.description: How the layout was chosen. Registered values: 'symbol' (a symbol table resolved the discriminant), 'configured' (an operator named it), 'fallback' (nothing resolved and the server guessed). Free string for `engine`'s reason. A server that answers 'fallback' MUST also emit `caveat`.

detectedFrom.description: The symbol whose resolution decided the layout, when detectedBy is 'symbol'. A symbolName, so it round-trips through emulator/lookup_symbol (§4).

slotBytes.description: Stride of one record in bytes. D9 category 2.

slotCount.description: Total slots the pool spans - what a full scan would cover. NOT the number of active objects, which is the reply's `total`.

baseAddr.description: Bus address of slot 0 (D9 category 1). Lets a client verify every item's addr with one multiplication, which is P1: a decoder reply must be checkable against another instrument on the same bus.

pools.description: The pool vocabulary AS DATA rather than as a schema enum, because an enum would freeze one engine's pool structure into the bus - D-27's stated objection. Ascending firstSlot, contiguous, covering [0, slotCount) where present at all. Absent on an engine with no pool structure. There is deliberately no per-item `pool` key: it is slot vs this table, the derivable key CR-13 struck (the sprites.parsedMax precedent).

decoderLayout.description: protocol.md §11.25 (CR-D). What the server decoded against, and how - REQUIRED on every reply from a decoder row, never in the handshake, because emulator/load_symbols may be called at any point in a session and the detect branches on whether a symbol resolves, so a handshake-time value is stale by construction. Closed here: it has no allOf for additionalProperties to be blind past (the otherMatches.items[] precedent).

decodedSlot.description: protocol.md §11.25 (CR-D). One decoded object record. A SHAPE LIBRARY: types only, deliberately UNCLOSED and carrying NO `required`, because a use-site additionalProperties:false beside allOf is blind past the allOf in BOTH directions and would refuse these very keys (§11.5). Each use site re-lists every permitted key name in its own `properties` (inherited keys as `true`, its additions typed), declares its own `required`, and closes itself. The `object_slot` result is the exception: it is a RESULT top level, where the closure is item 20's harness-side unevaluatedProperties - which does see through allOf - so it declares no additionalProperties at all.

slot.description: Index into the pool. D9 category 2. Sparse on object_list: empty slots are omitted, so slot numbers skip.

addr.description: Bus address of the record (D9 category 1). P1: the key that makes the entry checkable with emulator/read and pokeable with emulator/write_memory. The legacy server emits this on object_slot and player_state but NOT on object_list, which is why an object_list reply is unverifiable today.

x.description: World PIXELS, signed - the integer half of the record's position. Pixels rather than the engine's fixed-point word because pixels are the one value comparable ACROSS layouts; carrying a 16.16 raw would push one engine's fixed-point convention into the bus. A client wanting sub-pixels asks for the field by name or reads the bytes at addr.

code.description: The engine's identity datum for the slot, EXACTLY AS READ, at the offset and width the layout declares. A hex string (D9 category 1) on the sprites.satBase pattern: the representation is category 1 while the computation `ObjCodeBase + code` is what category 2 permits a client to do after parsing. Not a resolved address, because a layout whose identity datum is an object id rather than a code offset has no address to resolve, and a REQUIRED key meaningless on half the layouts is the freezing D-27 forbids. It is also the DISCRIMINANT that says how the record's overlay tail may be read.

name.description: The BARE label the server resolved for `code`. §4's identifying spelling: it MUST round-trip through lookup_symbol, so a suffix MUST NOT be stripped for display. Omitted when nothing resolved - never the empty string.

nameDisp.description: Bytes past `name`. Present with `name`. §4: 'A displacement is never inside a name string.'

fields.description: TYPED-OPEN MAP. Keys are the LAYOUT's own field names, never names this contract chose; values are scalars. Present iff the request asked for fields. The openness is a declared property of the shape, not a gap the harness fails to reach - the methodSummaries pattern, where the schema pins the value type and prose pins the key provenance. Prose obligations no schema can carry (§11.25): a server MUST NOT emit a key its layout.engine does not name; MUST NOT emit decoded bit-name enums; MUST omit or caveat a key that is addressable but not LIVE for the slot's current occupant; and a value follows D9 - address-shaped fields as hex strings, counts and scalars as numbers, per the layout's own typing of the field.

bytes.description: The whole record verbatim, slotBytes long. Present iff includeBytes. Off by default so the default reply's key set stays fully enumerated by this fragment.

objectAtBody.$comment: protocol.md §11.26 (CR-F). The object_at reply body, shared verbatim by the emulator/clicked event's params (M4). Authored by the oracle lane (oracle 2c1e5de, docs/proposed/2026-08-29-cr-f-s1-fragments.json) and applied by the contract lane; every iff the ruling states is enforced as if/then/else here, not described. Known residue, recorded so a green run is not read as coverage: M2's rule that a server MUST answer 'unavailable' (never 'none') when Sprite_Owner does not resolve, and M3's re-resolve-by-symbol rule, are SERVER BEHAVIOUR a document schema cannot see; both {kind:'unavailable'} and {kind:'none', raw:'0x0000'} are valid documents. Their tests are oracle conformance rows (a release ROM click asserting 'unavailable'; a romReloaded re-resolve), which land with the serve.

dot.description: §11.26 M1: the params echoed, so a reply stands alone in a log.

world.description: §11.26 M3: act-world = UNBIASED Camera_X + dot.x, Camera_Y + dot.y. Present iff worldSource == 'camera' (enforced below).

worldSource.description: §11.26 M3: independent of the owner half, so a build that can answer one and not the other answers the one it can.

layer.description: The displayed layer. camelCase values, matching the `runTo`/`runToScanline` stopped-reason spelling (protocol.md §3).

spriteIndex.description: SAT slot of the winning sprite. Present if and only if `layer` is 'sprite'. A slot index — D9 category 2.

kind.description: §11.26 M2: five outcomes. 'none' = the owner table exists and this entry is 0x0000; 'unavailable' = the loaded build has no owner table (Sprite_Owner does not resolve on its listing). They MUST NOT merge; a server MUST answer 'unavailable' when the symbol does not resolve.

raw.description: §11.26 M5: the owner word as read, served for AUDITING ONLY; a client MUST NOT rebase it (the sentinel guard exists once, on the server). Absent iff kind == 'unavailable': no table, no word.

allOf.$comment: §11.26 M1: spriteIndex present iff the winner is a sprite (mirrors pixel_attribution's winner).

stopPrecision.description: The relationship between a reported stop `pc` and the condition that halted the machine (protocol.md §2.1, §11.31). Totally ordered, strongest first: `exact` (the instruction at pc has not executed and, where the stop had a triggering address, pc IS it) > `afterCommit` (the instruction immediately before pc caused the stop and has fully committed; read state as post-trigger) > `approximate` (the server promises nothing about which side of the trigger pc is on, or by how much). One $def referenced from the handshake map and the stopped event, because a copied enum is a drift source.

serverName.description: Deployment label. MAY be config-set, so it MUST NOT be used to discriminate implementations — use `implementation` (protocol.md §2.1, added 2026-08-26 by §11.23). Two processes of the same implementation on one machine legitimately want distinguishable names, which is the job this field keeps.

serverVersion.description: Human-facing release label, REQUIRED since 2026-08-26 (protocol.md §2.1, §11.23). Clients MUST NOT branch on it, parse it, or order it; no format is defined. Build identity is `serverBuild`; implementation identity is `implementation`.

implementation.description: Which implementation of this contract answered (protocol.md §2.1, added 2026-08-26 by §11.23). THE REGISTRY IN protocol.md §2.1 GOVERNS and is extended only by amendment; this enum mirrors it so an unregistered value fails validation as well as prose, and a schema release follows an amendment to that table rather than leading one. NOT config-settable, and distinct from `serverName`, which is a deployment label.

id.description: Opaque build identifier, fixed when the binary was produced. Compare for equality only — never parse, order, or range-check. Differs between any two builds whose observable bus behaviour can differ, which under 'vcs' includes build configuration that changes the served surface (protocol.md §2.1).

source.description: How `id` was derived. 'declared' is a self-report and is typed as one on purpose (protocol.md §2.1). 'vcs' ids are derived from, not equal to, a revision: build configuration that changes the served surface is part of the id (protocol.md §2.1).

dirty.description: Uncommitted changes were present in the built sources. REQUIRED when source is 'vcs': a commit hash from a dirty tree names a commit whose content is not what was built. It covers uncommitted source only — build configuration rides inside `id` (protocol.md §2.1).

serverBuild.description: protocol.md §2.1 (added 2026-08-26 by §11.23). Which BUILD is answering, as distinct from which implementation. Structurally emitted, never read at run time: the value is fixed when the binary is produced and MUST be recomputed whenever the revision, the dirty state, or the surface-changing build configuration changes.

objectDecoders.description: Whether THIS BUILD has the object-decoder handlers - never whether a layout was detected. True iff AT LEAST ONE of the §6 decoder rows (object_slot, object_list, player_state) appears in `methods`; per-row servedness is `methods` membership and nothing else (§8 item 23), which this flag never overrides or summarises. Kept a boolean rather than promoted to an object: changing a published key's JSON type is not additive (§11.18), and checkpoints/watchpoints were BORN objects, so they are precedent for new keys and not for retyping an old one. The detect result travels on every decoder reply as `layout`, because emulator/load_symbols may be called at any time and a handshake-time detect is stale by construction. A client that branched on this flag to decide whether a decode would succeed would be reading a build-time constant as a run-time fact. protocol.md §11.25.

sixButtonPad.description: Whether this server models a 6-button pad. When false, `x`/`y`/`z`/`mode` are REFUSED with -32602 on every method that takes `buttons` — refused rather than silently ignored, because a caller who asked for a button that was dropped cannot tell that from a button the game ignored. Registered 2026-08-16 (§11.11): the reference server has advertised this key since the input methods shipped, while the schema's `buttons` enum accepted the names it refuses.

breakpoints.description: Whether the breakpoint family (§6) is served.

batch.description: Whether the server accepts batched requests (§2).

cap.description: Max live checkpoints; the server refuses at this count with -32005 (D13 rule 3).

checkpoints.description: protocol.md §6.1. An object, not a bare flag, because the cap must be discoverable before a client plans around it.

spaces.description: Which address spaces this server can watch. Advertised rather than assumed: a server with no VDP-internal write capture supports only 'bus', and a client must not have to arm a watch to find out.

maxWatches.description: Max live watches; the server REFUSES at this count with -32005 {reason:'watchCapReached', cap, count} (protocol.md §6, D13 rule 3 applied here). It never silently grows past it and never silently evicts, because a handle a client still holds must not quietly start meaning nothing.

ringCap.description: Capacity of the hit ring, in hits. Discoverable BEFORE a client plans around it, for D13's reason: past this the oldest hits are dropped (and counted by watchpoint_hits.dropped), so a client sweeping a hot range needs the number in advance, not after losing evidence to it. 0 is legal and means record nothing — a pure census configuration.

watchpoints.description: protocol.md §6. An object, not a bare flag, for the reason D13 gives checkpoints.cap: a client that has to hit a limit to learn it is a client that loses evidence finding out.

methods.description: Authoritative live method set — replaces the removed list_ops (D4). This array IS the count of the server's surface; no number in prose tracks it.

maxRunFrames.description: Largest `frames`/`maxFrames` this server accepts on a run-shaped op.

maxReadLen.description: Largest `len` this server accepts on a read-shaped op.

maxLineBytes.description: Largest single NDJSON line this server accepts (protocol.md §7.1) before refusing it.

maxInputRows.description: Largest `rows` count `emulator/play_input` accepts. Discoverable for the reason the checkpoint cap is: a client that must hit a limit to learn it is a client that loses the work it was doing when it found out.

maxWriteLen.description: Byte ceiling for one emulator/write_memory payload. REQUIRED when the server advertises emulator/write_memory.

maxHashLen.description: Byte ceiling for one emulator/memory_hash range. REQUIRED when the server advertises emulator/memory_hash.

maxBreakpoints.description: Max live breakpoints; the server REFUSES at this count with -32005 {reason:'breakpointCapReached', cap, count} and MUST NOT silently grow past the advertised number (protocol.md §6's breakpoint prose, added 2026-08-26 by §11.21, on the checkpoints.cap / watchpoints.maxWatches precedent — a client that has to hit a limit to learn it is a client that loses evidence finding out). OPTIONAL, and its absence is meaningful: a server that omits it serves the PRE-AMENDMENT breakpoint shape (§11.21 design choice 3). It rides `limits` rather than widening capabilities.breakpoints, which is a boolean shipping clients already parse and which §11.18 therefore forbids turning into an object.

maxProfilerRoutines.description: Largest `top` emulator/get_profiler_frames accepts, and the ceiling it applies to routines.items. REQUIRED when the server advertises emulator/get_profiler_frames (added 2026-08-19, §11.16, on the maxWriteLen/maxHashLen precedent). A POLICY bound, so it is advertised rather than discovered by refusal — the bound itself is refused, never clamped (§6's profiler blockquote).

maxProfilerFrames.description: Depth of the per-frame ring: the largest `frames` emulator/get_profiler_frames accepts and the most per-frame rows it retains while armed with set_profiler{perFrame:true}. REQUIRED when the server advertises emulator/get_profiler_frames (added 2026-08-19, §11.16). Bounding the ring is what keeps an opt-in per-frame record from growing without limit across a long sample; the aggregate figures are unaffected by it, since they accumulate in place rather than out of the ring.

maxProfilerCallers.description: Largest `topCallers` emulator/get_profiler_frames accepts, and the ceiling it applies to each routine row's `callers` list (added 2026-08-21, §11.18, on the maxProfilerRoutines precedent). A REPLY bound, not a retention bound: the accumulator keeps every observed call edge, which is what makes a row's `callersTotal` the true count of distinct callers rather than the count that survived a cap — the opposite of maxProfilerFrames, which really is a ring depth. Refused, never clamped. ITS PRESENCE IS THE CAPABILITY SIGNAL for the caller lens: a server that supports set_profiler{callers:true} MUST advertise this key, and a server that does not MUST omit it, so a client branches on capability rather than on a version integer (D5). That conditional requirement is prose here for the reason maxWriteLen's is — limits.required cannot express `required iff the server implements a lens`.

maxObjectSlots.description: Largest `limit` emulator/object_list accepts - THIS SERVER's ceiling, not the catalog's, on the maxProfilerRoutines / maxBreakpoints precedent. A POLICY bound, so it is advertised rather than discovered by refusal, and the bound itself is refused rather than clamped (-32602). OPTIONAL, and its absence is meaningful: a server that applies no ceiling omits it and object_list.limit is then bounded only by layout.slotCount. Optional rather than required because a decoder-less build has no such number and must not be made to invent one. Added 2026-08-26, §11.25.

limits.description: REQUIRED (protocol.md §2.1, §11.5). THIS SERVER's ceilings, not the catalog's: §6's parenthetical defaults describe the catalog, while a server hosted inside a player window legitimately runs a far lower maxRunFrames and REFUSES above it rather than clamping (§5). A client has no other way to discover that number, and discovering it by being refused is discovering it too late. The values MUST be the ones the server's own parameter checks actually enforce.

methodSummaries.description: OPTIONAL (protocol.md §2.1, §11.5), and its derivation clause is the whole condition of its existence: a server advertising it MUST derive it from the same registry as `methods`, its key set MUST equal `methods`, its values are non-normative prose, and clients MUST NOT use it for capability discovery — that is `methods` (D4), which exists because hand-maintained op inventories drift.

standard.description: Video standard, lowercase. Defined values today: 'ntsc', 'pal'. Deliberately not an enum — a client SHOULD branch on the numbers below, and the label exists so a human reading a log knows what they are looking at.

mclkPerFrame.description: Master-clock ticks in one frame — the divisor that turns an mclk stamp into a frame index (896040 NTSC).

linesPerFrame.description: Scanlines in one frame, including blanking (262 NTSC).

timingBasis.description: REQUIRED (protocol.md §2.1, D16). What the `frame` in every stamp MEANS. A top-level key rather than a capability flag: it is not something a server may or may not support, it is what that server's stamps are expressed in. The numbers are normative, not just the label ('ntsc' alone does not say 262 lines or 263), and a server MUST derive them from the same constants its own frame arithmetic uses.

stopPrecision.description: protocol.md §2.1 (§11.31, CR-E): one entry per `emulator/stopped` reason this server can emit, no more and no fewer, each the WEAKEST precision it may emit for that reason. OPTIONAL, and its absence is meaningful: a server that omits it serves the pre-amendment shape and does NOT answer the question. A client MUST NOT read absence as `exact`. Every event value must be at least as strong as the entry here (the binding rule), which relates two messages and is therefore held by §8 item 24, not by this fragment.

events.$comment: Event names are camelCase (romReloaded, never rom_reloaded) — protocol.md §3 and §10 decision 4. Every event's params also carries the machine stamp.

allOf.$comment: protocol.md §6: `watch` is REQUIRED when reason is 'watchpoint' and absent otherwise. Unlike `buttons`/`port` that rule DOES have a discriminator in the event itself, so it is enforced here rather than only in prose.

protocol.md §6's breakpoint prose, added 2026-08-26 by §11.21: `breakpoint` is REQUIRED when reason is 'breakpoint' and absent otherwise — the same discipline `watch` carries above, for the same reason, since the event carries its own discriminator. `reason` already contained 'breakpoint'; what it never carried was the handle naming WHICH breakpoint halted the machine, which is the whole point of §11.21 giving the surface one.

frames.description: Frames actually advanced. REQUIRED when reason is runFrames (protocol.md §3).

deadlineReached.description: True when the run ended on its bound rather than its condition (D12). Always true for runFrames.

buttons.description: The buttons held across the advance. REQUIRED when the advance was driven by emulator/press, absent otherwise (protocol.md §3). `reason` names the stop CONDITION and never the method, so this is where the stream learns that an input was injected — the half a subscriber that was not the caller cannot otherwise recover.

port.description: Which controller the buttons were held on. REQUIRED alongside `buttons` and absent without it: a partial attribution is worse than none, because a subscriber reading the stream in a two-pad session would attribute the input to the wrong pad.

watch.description: The watch whose `stopAfter` ended the run. REQUIRED when `reason` is 'watchpoint', absent otherwise (protocol.md §6). An opaque handle (D9 category 4) — the same one watchpoint_add issued and every hit carries — so a free-run halt always names its cause instead of leaving a client to guess which armed watch fired.

breakpoint.description: The breakpoint that halted the machine. REQUIRED when `reason` is 'breakpoint', absent otherwise (protocol.md §6's breakpoint prose, §11.21). An opaque handle (D9 category 4) — the same one emulator/breakpoint_add issued — so a halt names its cause instead of leaving a client to guess which armed breakpoint fired. Names exactly ONE: when several enabled breakpoints share the firing address the machine halts once and this is the EARLIEST-ADDED enabled one, while EVERY enabled breakpoint at that address increments its `hits`. Additive: a server serving the pre-amendment address surface emits no handle, and a client tells the two apart by emulator/breakpoint_set_enabled's presence in the handshake `methods` list.

stopPrecision.description: REQUIRED on every stopped event, for every reason (protocol.md §3, §11.31): the event always carries a pc, so it always has a precision. Reasons with no triggering address (pause, entry, runFrames) report `exact`. Must be at least as strong as the handshake declaration for this reason. A pre-amendment (legacy) server emits none and is not validated by this fragment for this event: frozen, not conformed (§11.21's disposition).

params.$comment: protocol.md §3: `buttons` and `port` are REQUIRED when the bounded frame advance was driven by emulator/press and absent otherwise. Only half of that is mechanically enforceable — `reason` names the stop CONDITION and never the driving method, so a press-driven advance and a run_frames one both read `runFrames` and the event carries no discriminator to key an if/then on. What IS enforceable, and is enforced by dependentRequired, is that the two travel together: a partial attribution would tell a subscriber in a two-pad session which buttons went down and not which pad.

buildId.description: reserved for the future build manifest

emulator/clicked.$comment: protocol.md §3 / §11.26 M4: emitted ONLY for a click the person made at the window, never for a method call. params = the object_at result body for that dot, verbatim, plus the stamp.

methods.$comment: THE TWELVE FRAGMENTS ADDED 2026-08-15 (protocol.md §11.5) — emulator/status, load_symbols, pause, resume, press, hold, release_all, read_vram, reload_rom, run_frames, screenshot, state_hash — were each written FROM THE AMENDED §6 ROW, never from a server's replies. That direction is the whole point: §8 forbids the emulator side to invent, and a fragment transcribed from what a server emits would encode the implementation as the contract, which is the inversion this document exists to prevent (§0: 'the contract leads; the emulator implements against it'). Where a shipped key had no §6 row it was ruled first — registered, pinned, or struck — and only then schematized.

emulator/status.$comment: protocol.md §6 (status / misc). `running` is NOT declared here: it is the machine stamp's (§2.2, D11), applied envelope-level after the handler returns and arriving through replyFields. §6's row lists it because the row predates D11; §2.2 is explicit that clients MUST NOT treat the stamp as a per-method field. Declaring it twice would invite a handler to think it owns the value.

frameToken.description: A JSON number under D9 category 2, and checked to be one: it is the emulated frame index, not a UI counter (protocol.md §11.2's 'what this pass deliberately did not change'). NOT a handle.

symbolAtPc.$comment: The BARE label at the PC — protocol.md §4's naming rule, which binds every symbol field on this bus. The displacement is `symbolDisp` and appears nowhere else; a rendering like 'Obj_Spring+$4' is the two fields concatenated, and a client that wants it can build it.

symbolDisp.description: Registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5). Bytes past `symbolAtPc`; 0 is an exact hit. Present when symbolAtPc is.

romBytes.description: Size of the loaded cartridge image. Registered 2026-08-15.

romPath.description: Path to the loaded ROM on the SERVER's filesystem — a host-filesystem fact, which D8's trusted-local-developer trust model makes unremarkable (see §6's paths note). Null when no ROM has been loaded from a path.

symbolsPath.description: Path to the loaded listing on the SERVER's filesystem, resolved to an absolute path by the same one rule as romPath at the load boundary (§6 paths note and its §11.30 rider): resolve where a file exists, pass the string through where none does. Never relative to the server's working directory, which no consumer can know. Null when no listing is loaded.

caveat.description: protocol.md section 2.4. Added 2026-09-04 (section 11.34, oracle CR-K): the standing symbol-freshness verdict. Emitted when the server cannot show that the listing at symbolsPath still parses to exactly the rows it holds: the file parses to different rows (rebuilt under the session), cannot be read, no longer parses as a listing, or a table is held with no recorded path. Quiet means only that the file has not moved past the table, never that the table is right for this image (load_symbols's own standard, one layer up). A client MUST NOT parse it (2.4 rule 3); a typed key is a separate amendment if a client ever needs to branch.

display.description: §11.29 rider (CR-H): whether a player window exists for emulator/screen_text to read. Optional and additive; a caller asks this rather than probing screen_text by failing. A headless server serves false.

emulator/load_symbols.$comment: protocol.md §4 and §6 (symbols). `binding` is §4's forward note, no longer forward.

path.description: The listing now loaded, spelled the way status.symbolsPath will spell it (absolute where a file exists; §11.30). One method never reports one file under two spellings in one exchange.

moduleCount.description: How many modules the listing spans, beside the symbol count. Registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5).

binding.description: Whether the listing could be checked against the ROM image actually loaded. `match` = it passed the check; `indeterminate` = it could not be checked at all and was accepted UNVERIFIED. There is deliberately no `mismatch` value: a listing that positively binds to a DIFFERENT image is refused with -32602 and carries its binding in error.data, because D7's hazard is that a mismatched listing is not degraded information but confidently wrong information.

caveat.description: protocol.md §2.4.

emulator/pause.$comment: protocol.md §6 (run-control). `wasRunning` registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5): it is D12's `reached` logic transposed — a result that reports nothing cannot distinguish 'I stopped it' from 'it was already stopped', and it is what lets a client make pause idempotent without a second round-trip.

wasRunning.description: Whether the machine was free-running BEFORE this call. Reports the transition, not the destination — the destination is known from the method name.

emulator/resume.$comment: protocol.md §6 (run-control). Mirror of emulator/pause; same field, same registration.

wasRunning.description: Whether the machine was free-running BEFORE this call.

emulator/reset.$comment: protocol.md §6 (run-control), result defined 2026-08-18 by §11.13 (CR-22) — the row predates the schema and its `deferred` key was never defined. NOT subject to the run-control state rule — it advances nothing and replaces state wholesale between frames, so it cannot fight the free-run loop — and it MUST NOT change the machine's run state (paused stays paused, free-running keeps running). The master clock restarts at 0, so stamps on subsequent replies jump backwards by design.

deferred.description: When the reset landed relative to this reply. false: applied before this reply was composed — every subsequent read on any connection sees the post-reset machine. true: accepted and handed to the thread that owns the machine without waiting for completion; it MUST land within a bounded time regardless of run state (a server that cannot bound it answers -32010 instead), and this reply's own stamp is pre-reset. Reports when it landed, never which thread applied it.

emulator/press.$comment: protocol.md §6 (input). Named in §6's run-control state rule: it mutates the timeline (it holds buttons across a bounded run of frames), so it requires a paused machine and MUST fail -32005 machineRunning otherwise.

frames.description: Catalog ceiling. A given server's ACTUAL ceiling is initialize's limits.maxRunFrames, which it refuses above rather than clamping to (§2.1).

port.description: Which controller. Registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5) — the two-controller surface the catalog never grew. D9 category 2 (an index a client counts with). Defaults to 0 so every call written before this row existed keeps meaning what it meant.

frames.description: Frames actually advanced, exact. Zero is reachable — see emulator/run_frames (§11.9).

port.description: Echoed on the result as well as accepted on the params: a reply that does not say which pad it acted on is unreadable in a two-client session, where the caller is not the only source of input.

emulator/hold.$comment: protocol.md §6 (input). NOT in the run-control state rule: hold sets pad state and advances nothing.

held.description: The buttons held on this port AFTER the call — the resulting set, not an echo of `buttons`. Registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5): hold has set-not-add semantics, and this is what makes that verifiable without a second round-trip. Deliberately NOT a boundedList: it is bounded at 8 by the controller, which is a structural bound (§2.4 clause (d)).

emulator/release_all.$comment: protocol.md §6 (input). NO RESULT KEYS, and that is a ruling rather than an omission: the reference server emitted `released: true`, a hardcoded constant that can never be false and carries zero bits, and it was REMOVED (§11.5) rather than registered. Removing it is not amputation — there was nothing attached. §6's row said `—` and still does, so this fragment is the row.

emulator/read_vram.$comment: protocol.md §6 (VRAM / CRAM / layers). The row is unchanged by this pass: its only surplus was a `caveat`, which §2.4 now defines once for the whole bus and which §2.4 clause 4 says a row need not enumerate. The fragment declares it anyway, because §8 item 20 closes results at test time and an undeclared caveat would fail that check.

caveat.description: protocol.md §2.4.

emulator/reload_rom.$comment: protocol.md §6 (run-control). Named in §6's run-control state rule — it swaps the cartridge out from under whatever is executing — so it requires a paused machine. Emits emulator/romReloaded. `wait` and `reset` were STRUCK 2026-08-20 (§11.17 postscript): both were carried from the legacy catalog as bare undescribed booleans, neither ever had a specified meaning, and the closure sweep that §2.5 made possible found that no server had ever read either. Serving a key whose semantics this document never stated would have been §8's invention ban; declaring one no handler reads is the silent-ignore §2.5 exists to end. They are now refused by name like any other undeclared key.

path.description: Omit to reload the image already loaded.

reloaded.description: The reload completed synchronously. Exactly one of `reloaded`/`queued` is present.

queued.description: The reload was accepted and will complete asynchronously; the romReloaded event is the completion signal.

romBytes.description: Size of the image now in the machine. Registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5), same key and same meaning as status.romBytes — it is the confirmation that the file read is the cartridge loaded.

symbolsDropped.description: The loaded symbol listing stopped binding to the new image and was dropped. Registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5), and it is the strongest registration in that pass: D7 is this contract's most emphatic decision, and a reload that silently invalidates the symbol table while a client keeps resolving names against it is precisely D7's named hazard. REQUIRED, present even when false — absence and false must not both mean 'your symbols are fine' (§2.3's argument).

caveat.description: protocol.md §2.4.

emulator/run_frames.$comment: protocol.md §6 (run-control) and §3. Requires a paused machine (-32005 machineRunning otherwise). Emits emulator/resumed, then emulator/stopped with reason 'runFrames' — NOT the nearest-looking 'step' (§8 item 13). This method's reply carried no surplus at all on the 2026-08-15 sweep, which §11.5 notes is not luck.

frames.description: Catalog default 1. The server's ceiling is initialize's limits.maxRunFrames, refused above rather than clamped.

Frames actually advanced, and it is EXACT — never rounded (protocol.md §6, §11.9). ZERO IS REACHABLE and is not an error: §11.8 gave a watch a `stopAfter`, so a bounded advance can end inside its own first frame, before one whole frame completed. The minimum was 1 until that amendment made 0 truthful, and a floor of 1 would have forced a server to report one frame it did not advance — a wrong number in the one case a caller most needs the right one.

emulator/screenshot.$comment: protocol.md §6 (status / misc). Five keys registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5) against a row that said only `path`. Neither this method nor reload_rom was reached by the ruling that opened that pass; both are ruled there.

path.description: Where to write. Omit and the server chooses; the chosen path is always echoed.

Where the image was written, absolute where the file exists (§6 paths note, §11.30 rider), including when the caller supplied a relative path; not absolute only by the accident of the default living in temp_dir().

format.description: The encoding written. A constant on any one server today and registered anyway — unlike the vacuous `released` struck from release_all, its value space is genuinely open, and §6's row already anticipates a second representation ('the HTTP binding MAY return image content inline'). A client that must infer the format from a file extension is guessing.

width.description: Not constant: H32 is 256 and H40 is 320, and a client indexing a pixel out of the file gets it wrong on one of them.

bytes.description: Size written, on the checkpoint.bytes precedent — how a caller knows the write completed rather than merely that a path was chosen.

source.description: WHICH PICTURE WAS SERVED. `raster` = the frame the scanline path actually drew. `stateRender` = re-derived from VDP state as it stands now, the honest fallback before any whole frame has been drawn. Provenance, and the register case rather than a nicety: §6's pixel_attribution prose already spends a paragraph on why the two legitimately differ and why pausing does NOT reconcile them (measured over 17 test ROMs). A stateRender picture silently labelled as the frame is the silent wrong answer D11 exists to prevent.

caveat.description: protocol.md §2.4 — and this method is the shape §2.4's advisory says to copy: it warns only when `source` is stateRender, rather than emitting a constant string on every reply.

emulator/state_hash.$comment: protocol.md §6 (status / misc). The five fingerprints cover VDP state only.

result.$comment: §6's row spells each hash '16-hex FNV-1a'. Read through D9 category 1 — a hex value on this bus is a hex string — that is $defs/hex narrowed to exactly 16 digits, which is the pattern used below rather than a bare 16-character form.

framebuffer.$comment: Present if and only if the includeFramebuffer param was true.

framebufferSource.description: Which picture was hashed — the same enum and the same meaning as emulator/screenshot's `source`, registered in the same pass (§11.5) and for a sharper version of the same reason: a fingerprint whose input provenance is unstated is worse than one that is simply wrong, because two machines can disagree on it for a reason that has nothing to do with either machine. Present if and only if `framebuffer` is.

caveat.description: protocol.md §2.4.

emulator/lookup_equate.$comment: Added 2026-09-05 (protocol.md section 11.36, oracle CR-M): the listing's EQUATE TABLE in a namespace of its own, never folded into the symbol table. Measured on aeon s4.debug.lst: 742 equates, 3,014 labels, zero name collisions, and 631 of the 742 equate VALUES fall inside the cart window, so folding them into addr->name would make an equate whose value is $1800 indistinguishable from a label AT $1800 on every reverse-lookup path, present and future. A separate door makes that impossible rather than filtered. Scope: what the LISTING publishes; values the build supplies on the command line are not in the listing (sigil DEFINES-REACH-THE-LISTING, open).

name.description: Exact equate name. Absent from the Equate Table is -32013 (data.missing, the name); no listing loaded is -32012. Neither is confusable with a label miss: labels live in emulator/lookup_symbol.

prefix.description: Bounded prefix search over equate names, the ergonomic path a client already knows from lookup_symbol; the reply lists matches up to the server's bound and says whether it truncated.

name.description: The equate's name as the listing spells it (name form).

value.description: The equate's VALUE as a plain integer (D9 category 2: a number, never a hex string), which is NOT an address even when it falls inside the cart window; a client that wants to treat it as one does so on its own authority. Present with name on an exact hit.

query.description: The prefix that was searched (prefix form).

matches.description: Prefix form: the matching equates, name and value, bounded by the server; an empty array is a real answer (no equate starts with that prefix), not an error.

truncated.description: Prefix form: true when the server's bound cut the list; absent or false means the list is complete.

caveat.description: protocol.md section 2.4. The same standing symbol-freshness verdict emulator/status carries (11.34): emitted when the server cannot show the listing at symbolsPath still parses to the rows it holds.

result.$comment: protocol.md §4, rewritten 2026-08-15 (§11.5). The anyOf is §4's one structural invariant: a result MUST carry either `addr` or `otherMatches` — the call either resolved to a location or offers candidates, and a reply that does neither has answered nothing while reporting success. Nothing else is required across all three result shapes, so nothing else is listed as required here; the per-shape obligations are prose in §4, which D14 makes normative for semantics.

addr.$comment: The resolved bus address. Absent only on the prefix-fallback shape, where nothing was resolved and inventing one would be a silent wrong answer.

demangled.description: The readable spelling, for display to a human. Present when it differs from `name`. NOT guaranteed unique and NOT guaranteed to round-trip — `ambiguous` is how a server says so.

disp.description: Queried address minus the resolved symbol's address; 0 is an exact hit. Address direction only. This is the ONLY place the displacement appears — see `name`.

query.description: The `addr` or `name` the request asked for, echoed. Load-bearing rather than decorative: on the address direction the answer's `addr` is the SYMBOL's address, not the queried one, so without this the reply does not record what was asked; on the prefix shape it is the reply's only trace of the request. A string in both directions (a hex address is a string, D9 category 1).

exact.description: REQUIRED on the name direction and present in BOTH cases: true = a symbol has exactly this name, false = these are prefix guesses. Not omitted on the true branch — a field that appears only in the unusual case is a field nobody reads (D16's argument, and D17's).

ambiguous.description: Several DIFFERENT addresses share this symbol's demangled spelling, so the readable name does not identify a location. The machine-readable half of the corresponding caveat, and it exists because §2.4 forbids parsing the caveat.

synthetic.description: The resolved label is toolchain plumbing (an alignment pad, a synthetic block scope) rather than a name a person wrote. Address direction. A client showing a PC to a human needs to know the nearest label is a pad.

rawAddr.$comment: The listing's own unmasked spelling of `addr` where the two differ — a 68000 listing writes work RAM as 0xFFFF8CFA while the machine drives 24 address lines and puts 0x00FF8CFA on the bus. Carried so a client can round-trip a value back to the listing text. `addr` is the one to compute with: passing `rawAddr` to `read_memory` is refused loudly ("the 68000 bus is 24 bits wide"), so a joining client that takes the wrong field pays a round trip, never gets a wrong byte (oracle, 2026-08-29, found by hitting it).

caveat.description: protocol.md §2.4. Conditional here, correctly: it fires on a non-zero displacement, on an ambiguous readable name, and on the prefix fallback.

otherMatches.$comment: CR-14, adopted 2026-08-15. Was `{type: array, items: {type: string}}`, which the reference server had never emitted: a bare array is exactly what §2.4 clause (a) forbids on a method §4 itself says truncates at 5, and bare strings would drop the `addr` the client asked for. The bound is a POLICY bound (this spec chose 5; a symbol table holds thousands) so total/truncated are mandatory — and there is NO cursor and NO nextCursor, because lookup_symbol accepts no continuation param and §2.4 clause (b) forbids a token that can never be handed back. Symbol BROWSING, if ever wanted, is a new cursored method and its own change request; lookup_symbol is a resolution primitive.

name.$comment: Same contract as the top-level `name` — this is the value a client hands back to resolve the match, so it is the round-trippable spelling and not the readable one.

items.description: ONE pinned item shape. The reference server emitted two — {name,addr} on the exact-demangled branch and {name,demangled,addr} on the prefix branch — which is a client having to discover which branch it is on in order to read the list.

emulator/read.$comment: protocol.md §6 (memory), added 2026-08-16 by §11.12 (CR-20). ONE byte read across the four address spaces, taking emulator/watchpoint_add's `space` vocabulary UNCHANGED. The reason for the row is not the count of methods it absorbs: a cram/vsram watch hit reports `space`+`addr`, and before this row no method accepted that pair back — this is the read half of the watch surface. The Z80's space is deliberately NOT a value here; emulator/z80_read keeps its own row and its own bounds. A pure read: not subject to §6's run-control state rule. emulator/read_memory and emulator/read_vram are exact aliases of space bus/vram and are retained (D5, and a live client drives both by name).

space.description: Which address space, spelled exactly as emulator/watchpoint_add spells it. An unknown value is -32602.

addr.description: First byte to read, in `space`. D9 category 1.

symbol.description: Resolved to an address (D7). Valid ONLY with space 'bus' — a symbol names a 68000 address and a VDP-internal byte address has no symbol. Any other space with `symbol` is -32602.

len.description: Bytes to read. A base outside the space, or a range whose END runs past it, is -32004 — REFUSED, never clipped, because a clipped read reports bytes it never looked at. Space sizes: bus 24-bit, VRAM 0xFFFF, CRAM 0x7F, VSRAM 0x4F.

space.description: Echoed, so a reply is self-describing: `addr` means nothing without the space it is in.

region.description: Which region of the 68000 map the read landed in. Present IFF space is 'bus' — one region per VDP-internal space makes it meaningless there. Enforced in the schema rather than left to prose, in both directions (the `old`/`fc` precedent).

caveat.description: §2.4. Emitted CONDITIONALLY, never on every reply — a caveat every reply carries is one nobody reads. The debug-read property of these reads lives in the row's prose instead.

emulator/memory_hash.$comment: protocol.md §6 (memory), added 2026-08-18 by §11.13 (CR-23). Fingerprints a byte range without moving it — the gap state_hash leaves (its five hashes cover VDP state only). A pure read: a server MUST NOT refuse it on a free-running machine, and the sample is taken at a single coherent machine point. Two regions: work RAM ($E00000-$FFFFFF, mirror-masked) or cartridge ROM ($000000 up to romBytes); -32004 for a base in neither or a range crossing out of its region, refused never clipped. Distinct from §9's deferred frame_hash (a picture hash, served by state_hash includeFramebuffer). caveat is declared absent, not omitted by accident (the sprites precedent): no nameable weaker-answer condition.

addr.description: First byte to hash. D9 category 1.

symbol.description: Resolved to an address (D7); alternative to addr.

len.description: Bytes to hash. REQUIRED — a hash without a length hashes nothing. Bounded by limits.maxHashLen.

region.description: Which of the two regions answered — read_memory.region's spellings ('work RAM', 'cartridge ROM').

fnv1a64.description: FNV-1a, 64-bit parameters: offset basis 0xCBF29CE484222325, prime 0x100000001B3, folded over the range's bytes in ascending address order.

crc32.description: IEEE/zlib CRC-32, so a cartridge-window hash equals CRC32 over the same slice of the ROM file.

symbolDisp.description: Bytes past the resolved symbol. Present with `symbol`; per §4 the displacement lives in this number and NEVER inside the name string.

region.description: PROVENANCE, not decoration (protocol.md §6, §11.5): the region the bytes were actually taken from — 'work RAM', 'cartridge ROM', and whatever a wider map adds. An inspection read is a DEBUG read, taken straight out of the region and bypassing the bus, so which region answered is a fact about the answer rather than one derivable from the address. A client can derive it from `addr` ONLY against a fixed map, and the moment a cartridge mapper or a bank register enters the catalog that derivation is wrong while looking right.

caveat.description: §2.4's shared convention. Declared here because §8 item 20 closes results against their fragments, so a method that CAN emit a caveat must declare it or its own conformant reply is rejected.

emulator/write_memory.$comment: protocol.md §6 (memory), specified 2026-08-18 by §11.13 (CR-21). The poke primitive. Work-RAM window $E00000-$FFFFFF only, refused (-32004) never clipped; exactly one payload spelling (bytes XOR value+width, else -32602), enforced mechanically below; a payload over limits.maxWriteLen is -32602, refused never truncated; requires a paused machine per the §6 run-control state rule (-32005 machineRunning). Values land big-endian. A poke is never offered to the watch surface: a hit's pc names the instruction that drove the access, and a poke has none to name. The keep-dead 'register-write op' entry was ruled (2026-08-17) to cover register writes only. caveat is declared absent, not omitted by accident (the sprites precedent): neither refusal has a nameable weaker-answer condition.

addr.description: First byte to write. D9 category 1.

symbol.description: Resolved to an address (D7); alternative to addr.

disp.description: Byte displacement added to the address `symbol` resolves to (protocol.md §2.5, added 2026-08-19 by §11.17). Valid ONLY with `symbol` — with `addr` it is arithmetic the caller has already done — and the dependentRequired above makes {addr, disp} -32602. Non-negative because it mirrors the `symbolDisp` a read reply hands back, which is a displacement from the NEAREST PRECEDING symbol and cannot be negative: {symbol, symbolDisp} out, {symbol, disp} in, which is D7's round trip made literal. The displaced address must still land in the work-RAM window (-32004 otherwise), and the reply's `addr` echoes the resolved, displaced address.

bytes.description: Byte payload — hex string, even digit count enforced by the pattern (D9 category 1). Alternative to value+width; passing both is -32602.

value.description: Numeric payload; must fit width. Requires width.

width.description: Byte width of value. Valid only with value.

emulator/read_cram.$comment: protocol.md §6 (VRAM / CRAM / layers), specified 2026-08-19 by §11.17 (CR-27). This row's FIRST fragment: it was catalogued from the legacy socket and never schematized, which is why it could not be served — §8 item 20 closes results against fragments, so a method without one would ship a result nobody had checked. The whole palette or one line of it: `line` omitted returns all 64 entries and is ABSENT from the reply, `line` given returns that line's 16 and is ECHOED, and the echo<->length tie is enforced by the result's if/then in both directions (the `read` region precedent). A pure read: a server MUST NOT refuse it on a free-running machine, exactly as read, sprites, pixel_attribution and scanlines. `palette` is STRUCTURALLY bounded (4x16 by the video hardware), so it takes neither total/returned/truncated nor a cursor (§2.4 clause (d), pixel_attribution's `candidates` precedent). Entries carry the STORED colour — r/g/b are emulator/write_cram's 0-7 components and `raw` the stored word — never a displayed one: pixel_attribution.rgb is the displayed colour and the two differ whenever `state` is not 'normal'. No 8-bit expansion is emitted: this catalog has never pinned an intensity ramp, and the two servers that compute one disagree (the legacy socket bit-replicates, the reference server runs level*255/7 — one apart at levels 2, 4 and 6), so an unpinned number two conformant servers answer differently is worse here than an absent one. caveat is declared ABSENT, not omitted by accident (the sprites precedent): reading live CRAM has no weaker-answer condition to warn about.

line.description: Palette line to read. Omitted: all four lines, 64 entries. Outside 0-3 is -32602 — refused, never clipped. An index, so a JSON number (D9 category 2).

allOf.$comment: The echo and the length are tied in BOTH directions: 16 entries iff `line` is echoed, 64 iff it is not. The `read` fragment's region-present-iff-bus if/then is the precedent, and the reason is the same — a client must be able to tell which of the two answers it is holding without counting an array.

line.description: Echoed IFF the param was given. Its presence is what says which of the two answers this is.

palette.description: The requested entries, line-ascending then index-ascending, contiguous. Structurally bounded, so no total/returned/truncated and no cursor (§2.4 clause (d)); the length is fixed by the request and a partial list is not expressible.

line.description: Palette line. Carried on every entry, the single-line answer included, so one entry on its own addresses the same cell through emulator/write_cram.

index.description: Index within the line — emulator/write_cram's `index`, so the (line,index) pair hands straight back.

cramAddr.$comment: CRAM byte address of the entry, (line*16 + index)*2. Derivable, and carried anyway because it is the JOIN key three other surfaces speak and (line,index) is not: pixel_attribution.cramAddr, the space+addr pair a cram watch hit reports, and emulator/read with space 'cram'. pixel_attribution's cramIndex is NOT carried — it is line*16 + index, and that method emits it only because it has no (line,index) pair to give (emulator/sprites' omitted per-entry satAddr is the same rule reaching the opposite answer for the opposite reason).

raw.description: The stored CRAM word, masked to the 9-bit colour (0x0EEE, ---- BBB- GGG- RRR-). D9 category 1.

r.description: Stored red component, 3-bit — emulator/write_cram's `r`. A component, so a JSON number (D9 category 2). NOT the displayed colour; see pixel_attribution.rgb.

emulator/write_cram.$comment: protocol.md §6 (VRAM / CRAM / layers), amended 2026-08-19 by §11.17 (CR-27). This fragment came from the ORIGINAL Phase-1 contract commit and no CR had touched it since: it predates §11.5's result-key pass, §2.4's conventions and §8 item 20's closure, and it showed. Three defects are now mechanical. (1) The result declared no `required`, and item 20's closure catches a SURPLUS key while saying nothing about a MISSING one — so a reply carrying nothing beyond the envelope fields, with no cramAddr and no value, passed the gate, on a row whose whole job is to confirm where the write landed. (A LITERAL {} was refused by both revisions, since replyFields and the stamp are required through the allOf; the defect was that the two write-confirming keys were optional.) (2) `raw` was an unbounded integer against a 9-bit chip. (3) The r/g/b-vs-raw alternation the §6 row states was enforced nowhere: both at once passed, and so did a lone `r`. The alternation is now a oneOf plus a dependentRequired over the triple (emulator/write_memory's bytes-XOR-value+width precedent), and the result requires all four keys, `line`/`index` echoed so a reply is self-describing — cramAddr alone makes a client recompute its own request to confirm it (the `read` echo precedent). Requires a paused machine per the §6 run-control state rule (-32005 machineRunning). Prose-only, because JSON Schema's integer keywords cannot express it: a `raw` carrying bits outside the 0x0EEE mask is -32602, REFUSED and never masked — the coarser bound below is the mechanical half, exactly as write_memory's `value` is bounded 0..2^32-1 with must-fit-`width` left to the server. caveat is declared ABSENT, not omitted by accident (the sprites and write_memory precedent): the poke's two standing properties — never offered to the watch surface, and no repaint of an already-drawn frame — are stated once in §6 rather than repeated on every reply (§2.4's advisory against the constant caveat, and §11.15's own reason for stating a standing property in the document).

line.description: Palette line. Outside 0-3 is -32602 — refused, never clipped. An index, so a JSON number (D9 category 2).

index.description: Index within the line. Outside 0-15 is -32602 — refused, never clipped.

r.description: Stored red component, 3-bit. Travels with g and b — a partial triple is -32602 — and the triple and `raw` are alternatives, so passing both is -32602 too.

g.description: Stored green component, 3-bit. Travels with r and b.

b.description: Stored blue component, 3-bit. Travels with r and g.

raw.description: The whole stored word as a number: at most 0x0EEE (---- BBB- GGG- RRR-). Alternative to r/g/b, and passing both is -32602. A value with bits outside that mask is -32602 — refused, never masked — which this bound alone cannot express.

line.description: Echoed, so the reply is self-describing without the client re-deriving its own request from an address.

cramAddr.description: CRAM byte address written, (line*16 + index)*2 — the spelling emulator/read_cram's entries, pixel_attribution and a cram watch hit all use. D9 category 1.

value.description: The word ACTUALLY STORED — the masked 9-bit colour, so a client reads back what the chip holds rather than what it sent.

emulator/registers.$comment: protocol.md §6 (memory & Z80). PROPERTIES ADDED 2026-08-15 (§11.5): this fragment previously declared NONE, and stood in for them with `additionalProperties: {$ref hex}` plus a hand-listing of the four envelope fields to stop that catch-all rejecting them. The catch-all is gone with the properties: it was open in the direction that mattered (any misspelled register name passed, so long as its value looked like hex) and closed in the direction D5 protects (a future registered non-hex key would have been rejected). Enumerating the file is what makes `usp`/`ssp` — registered in the same pass — checkable at all.

result.description: The 68000 architectural register file: d0–d7, a0–a7, pc, sp, usp, ssp, sr — every one a hex string (D9 category 1). The envelope fields (§2.2 stamp, §2.3 droppedEvents) arrive through replyFields and are numbers/booleans; they are NOT listed here, because nothing in this fragment rejects them any more.

a7.$comment: A7 is the ACTIVE stack pointer — the same value as `sp` — because the 68000 selects between usp and ssp by the S bit. Both spellings are carried because both are how people read a register dump; `usp` and `ssp` below are the two banks unconditionally, which is the fact a7/sp cannot express while the S bit is unknown to the reader.

usp.description: User stack pointer, registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5). Named because the active `sp`/`a7` is only one of the two banks and a debugger cannot tell which without decoding the S bit out of `sr`.

ssp.description: Supervisor stack pointer. Same registration, same reason.

emulator/run_to.$comment: protocol.md D12 — bounded, and it says whether it fired.

maxFrames.description: Bound. Without it an unreachable target is an unbounded run (D12).

reached.description: True = the condition fired. False = the run ended on maxFrames; NOTHING about the machine state follows from where it stopped.

caveat.description: SHOULD be present when reached is false.

emulator/checkpoint.$comment: protocol.md §6.1 / D13 — volatile, whole-machine, capped, refused loudly.

label.description: Optional human string; carried back verbatim, never interpreted.

id.description: The checkpoint handle. Server-assigned, never client-proposed (no cross-client collisions), and an OPAQUE STRING per D9 category 4 — not a slot index. A client hands it back to restore/checkpoint_drop and does nothing else with it. Pinned 2026-08-15 (protocol.md §6.1, §11.2); a numeric id here is non-conformant however plausible D9's earlier wording made it.

bytes.description: Snapshot size, so a client can see the cap coming.

emulator/restore.$comment: Restores the WHOLE machine, ROM included (D13 rule 2). Unknown id => -32005 unknownCheckpoint.

cursor.description: A continuation handle previously returned by this method. Opaque (D9 category 4): the client hands it back unexamined. Its BEHAVIOUR is normative — stable under concurrent mutation, never skipping or repeating a live item (protocol.md §6.1) — while its representation is deliberately the server's.

result.$comment: §2.4's FLAT spelling of the bounded-list rule, used because the list here IS the whole result rather than a field of one: the same field set as $defs/boundedList, as siblings of the array instead of wrapped around it. total/returned/limit registered 2026-08-15 (§11.5). Deliberately not unified onto the nested container — see §2.4's closing paragraph, which is also the one point this amendment says it would not argue with an owner who unified it.

total.description: Live checkpoints in total, not on this page.

returned.description: checkpoints.length, restated so a client can compare it to `total` without counting.

limit.description: The page ceiling actually applied, which is not necessarily the one the client asked for — a server clamps this to its checkpoint cap.

cursor.description: Present when more remain. Opaque (D9 category 4) — pass it back as the `cursor` param, unexamined.

truncated.description: Bounded/cursored like every list on this bus — a client must never mistake a partial list for a complete one.

emulator/pixel_attribution.$comment: protocol.md §6 (VRAM/CRAM/layers). Answers 'why is the dot at (x,y) the colour it is' against the VDP's CURRENT state — the server re-derives the scanline per call and reads no framebuffer, so on a free-running machine the answer is a live sample and the envelope's `running: true` is what says so (D11). A pure read: NOT subject to §6's run-control state rule. §11.27: `caveat` declared; `rgb` stays the LIVE colour by contract, the caveat is the disclosure that the drawn picture may differ.

x.description: Screen column, 0-based (D9 category 2 — a position a client counts with, not an address). Bounded here at the widest addressable value; the ACTIVE bound is the `width` this method reports, and a dot outside it is refused with -32004.

y.description: Screen line, 0-based. Same category and the same treatment as `x` — D9 names `line` among the JSON numbers, and this is that field.

width.description: Active display width the coordinates were resolved against (256 H32 / 320 H40). Reported so a client can bound its own sweep without first provoking a -32004.

height.description: Active display height (224, or 240 in V30).

layer.description: The displayed layer. camelCase values, matching the `runTo`/`runToScanline` stopped-reason spelling (protocol.md §3).

spriteIndex.description: SAT slot of the winning sprite. Present if and only if `layer` is 'sprite'. A slot index — D9 category 2.

cramIndex.description: The DISPLAYED colour's CRAM entry (palette*16 + nibble; the backdrop register's value for a backdrop dot). An index — D9 category 2.

cramAddr.$comment: The CRAM byte address of that entry (index*2). An address — D9 category 1, and `cramAddr` is the spelling emulator/write_cram already uses.

rgb.description: The colour actually put on the glass: the 3-bit channels run through the intensity ramp at the resolved shadow/highlight `state`. NOT the stored CRAM components — emulator/write_cram's r/g/b (0-7) are the stored colour, this is the displayed one, and the two differ whenever `state` is not 'normal'. Components, so JSON numbers (D9 category 2); 0-255 because that is the range the ramp emits.

state.description: The resolved shadow/highlight state applied to this dot's intensity (never its identity).

tile.description: Pattern index. A JSON number (D9 category 2) and NOT a hex string: arithmetic on it is meaningful and load-bearing — tile*32 is the VRAM address, and a multi-cell sprite's dot is base+offset. D9's category-4 test is 'a type a client must never compute on'; this is the opposite of that.

tileAddr.$comment: VRAM byte address of that pattern (tile*32, wrapped into VRAM). The address form, so a client can feed it straight to emulator/read_vram. A pattern is 32 bytes and cannot straddle the 64 KB wrap, so this plus 32 is the whole range.

cell.description: The winning nametable entry, decoded. Present if and only if `winner.layer` is planeA, planeB or window — a sprite or backdrop dot has no nametable cell.

x.description: Screen X of the sprite's top-left, (Xfield & 0x1FF) - 128. Signed: a sprite scrolling in from the left is legitimately negative.

baseTile.description: The sprite's base pattern index from its attribute word.

tile.description: The pattern this DOT is drawn from — base + (col*heightCells) + row after flips, column-major, wrapping. ABSENT when the winning sprite's box no longer contains the dot, which means the SAT was rewritten between the render and this query; the server reports the absence rather than inventing a tile.

tileAddr.$comment: VRAM byte address of `tile`. Present exactly when `tile` is.
