satAddr.$comment: VRAM byte address of this sprite's 8-byte attribute-table entry (sat_base + index*8). This is the range a game writes when it moves, re-points or re-links the sprite — the answer to 'who MOVED this?' as opposed to 'who DREW this?'.

cacheDivergence.description: The cached Y/size/link disagree with VRAM at the current reg-5 base — the stale-SAT-cache state made visible (the Castlevania Bloodlines mixing). Present only when true.

sprite.description: The winning sprite, decoded. Present if and only if `winner.layer` is 'sprite'.

candidates.description: Every layer that could have shown at this dot, in VDP priority order, with why each won or lost. Deliberately NOT cursored: the list is bounded at 4 BY CONSTRUCTION (at most one flattened sprite pixel, the plane-A slot, plane B, and the backdrop), not by a server policy a client would have to page around. A live dot yields 3 or 4 entries; a BLANKED dot (display off, or the leftmost-column blank at x<8) yields exactly one — the backdrop, verdict 'won' — which is why minItems is 1 and not 3.

cramIndex.description: The colour this layer WOULD have shown.

verdict.description: won = displayed. lostToPriority = opaque, but outranked. transparent = colour nibble 0, contributes nothing. operator = an opaque sprite operator (palette 3, nibble 14/15) that outranks the winner but is not drawn — it shifted the winner's shadow/highlight state instead.

caveat.description: protocol.md §2.4. Registered §11.27: emitted when the CRAM entry at `cramIndex` has been written since line `y` of the last completed frame was drawn, or when no frame has completed, so the picture on the glass MAY disagree with `rgb`; it names `emulator/scanlines` as the reconciliation path. Never emitted unconditionally (§2.4 advisory); absent when no such write occurred.

emulator/play_input.$comment: protocol.md §6 (input), added 2026-08-16 by §11.11 (CR-19). The pad as a TIMELINE rather than as accumulated state. THE normative property, which the schema cannot express and the prose therefore carries: the pad at frame N is a pure function of `rows` and of NOTHING else — the client's held set and any host live input are both SUSPENDED for the duration and restored unchanged afterwards, and a port no row covers is fully released. Overlapping rows on one port UNION, order-independently, so rows need not be sorted or disjoint. Subject to §6's run-control state rule (-32005 while free-running). Does NOT subsume emulator/press: press UNIONS with session state, this REPLACES it. Not wait-shaped, so D12's `reached` does not apply.

rows.description: The timeline. Empty is -32602: a request to do nothing is refused rather than silently satisfied. The upper bound is this server's `limits.maxInputRows`.

start.description: First frame this row applies to, 0-based and relative to the call. A count, so a JSON number (D9 category 2).

end.description: One past the last frame this row applies to: the interval is half-open [start, end). `end <= start` is -32602 — an empty interval is a row that says nothing, and accepting it would let a script look like it did something it did not.

buttons.description: The buttons this row CONTRIBUTES (not a complete pad state — under union no single row is complete).

maxFrames.description: Frame ceiling for this call, bounded by `limits.maxRunFrames` — run_frames' own ceiling, NOT press's legacy 1000, which is far too short for the re-record workflow this method exists for. Absent, it is the largest `end`. Below the largest `end` it TRUNCATES, and rows starting at or beyond it never apply.

frames.description: Frames actually advanced. EXACT, including zero (§11.9) — a watch with `stopAfter` can end the run inside frame 0, and this is also the stop position, which is why no separate `stoppedAt` exists (§11.5's struck run_to.stoppedAtFrame).

emulator/sprites.$comment: protocol.md §6 (VRAM / CRAM / layers), added 2026-08-16 by §11.10 (CR-18) closing the last item-19 violation. The sprite attribute table AS A TABLE — the whole-machine reading, in slot order. Deliberately NOT the SAT's other reading, the per-scanline link walk, which reaches no panel and is therefore not in violation; it gets its own row when something renders it. A pure read: not subject to §6's run-control state rule, and emitting NO caveat, because the envelope's `running` is the whole answer to a torn sample (§2.4 rule 4 — declared absent, not omitted by accident). §2.4's flat bounded-list spelling, as `watchpoint_hits` uses it, with `satBase` and `parsedMax` as scalars beside the list. No cursor: the table is a fixed 80 entries and the method accepts no continuation (CR-14's ruling for `otherMatches`).

limit.description: Maximum entries to return, from slot 0 upward. Bounded at the table's own size: a limit that could exceed what exists would be a policy wearing a count's name. A count, so a JSON number (D9 category 2).

satBase.description: VRAM byte address of the sprite attribute table (reg $05, masked for the mode). D9 category 1. Emitted ONCE here rather than as a per-entry satAddr: each entry's address is satBase + index*8, which D9 category 2 explicitly permits a client to compute, and CR-13 struck result keys derivable from values already present.

parsedMax.description: How many slots the hardware would actually parse in the current mode: 80 in H40, 64 in H32. Slots at index >= parsedMax are returned anyway — they are really in VRAM, and clipping them would hide bytes the caller asked about — but the hardware never looks at them. On THIS reply rather than left to a second call, per D11. There is deliberately no per-entry `parsed` flag: it is index < parsedMax, the derivable key CR-13 struck.

total.description: The size of the table, ALWAYS 80. Never parsedMax (which is a hardware limit, not a table size) and never `returned`. Pinned as a const because an H32 server reporting 64 here is otherwise a defensible misreading.

limit.description: The page size in effect, echoed so a caller can tell a default from its own request. Bounded at the table's own size rather than the house 4096: this list cannot exceed 80, and a ceiling a list can never reach is two policies wearing one name (§11.8).

sprites.description: SLOT ORDER, index-ascending — NEVER link order. With no `limit`, entry i is slot i. Pinned because the SAT's other reading IS link-ordered, making this the one place two conformant servers could differ defensibly.

index.description: SAT slot, not link-walk position. A slot index, so a JSON number (D9 category 2).

x.description: Screen X = Xfield - 128. Legitimately NEGATIVE for a sprite entering from the left; that is not an error state and MUST NOT be clamped.

y.description: Screen Y = Yfield - 128, from the VDP's internal cache. Legitimately negative; see `x`.

link.description: Next sprite index in the link chain. Reported as decoded state; this row does not walk it.

baseTile.description: The sprite's base pattern index from its attribute word. Same spelling and same semantics as pixel_attribution.sprite.baseTile — two sprite decodes on one bus MUST NOT drift apart.

cacheDivergence.description: The cached Y/size/link disagree with VRAM at the current reg-5 base — the stale-SAT-cache state made visible, i.e. the difference between 'the game wrote the sprite' and 'the VDP will draw the sprite'. PRESENT ON EVERY ENTRY, false included: false is a real answer (the two agree), and a field that appeared only in the unusual case is a field nobody reads (§11.5's `exact` re-ruling). Deliberately the opposite convention from pixel_attribution.sprite.cacheDivergence, whose alignment to always-present is a registered follow-up.

emulator/scanlines.$comment: protocol.md §6 (VRAM/CRAM/layers), added 2026-08-18 by §11.14 (CR-24). Row-range readback of the most recently completed frame's rendered active display — the live raster, S/H applied, mid-frame effects included — never a post-hoc state render when a completed frame exists. A pure read: a server MUST NOT refuse it on a free-running machine, exactly as read and sprites. No frame param: drive the machine to F and read; the envelope stamp is the frame identity. Bounds are structural (active lines 0-223 — this catalog's slice is the NTSC V28 display; a V30-capable server needs a §11 amendment raising the bound): startLine+count past 224 is -32602, refused never clipped — a decision, not drift, versus pixel_attribution's -32004, whose bound is mode-dependent and not schema-expressible — and the list takes neither truncated nor cursor (§2.4: structural bound -> neither). source carries screenshot's spellings ('raster'|'stateRender'), where stateRender is the fallback when no completed frame is retained — before the first frame, and again after reset/reload_rom/restore drop it; a liveness-dependent gate MUST check source=='raster' — a stateRender row passes every shape check and is structurally blind to mid-frame effects. caveat is emitted on stateRender only — declared, not omitted by accident (the sprites precedent). The caveat<->source tie is deliberately left mechanically unenforced, matching screenshot's fragment, the direct precedent (CR-24 ruling disposition (a)). Prose-only, since JSON Schema cannot express them: startLine+count <= 224; rows contiguous and line-ascending; rows.length == count.

startLine.description: First active-display line to return. Default 0. D9 category 2.

count.description: Rows to return. Default: through line 223. startLine+count must not exceed 224 — refused (-32602), never clipped.

mode.description: The answering frame's width class: h40 = 320 px, h32 = 256 px. A mid-frame width switch is normalized to the width the frame ended on — shorter lines black-padded, longer lines cropped. A stateRender reply's mode is the width the VDP would draw now. The mode<->width<->rgb-length tie is enforced by the result's if/then.

source.description: Which instrument answered — screenshot's spellings. raster: the retained live per-line capture (the normative content). stateRender: the fallback when no completed frame is retained — before the first frame, or after reset/reload_rom/restore dropped it — rendered from current VDP state; structurally blind to mid-frame effects, so liveness gates MUST check for raster.

width.description: Pixels in this row. Equals mode's width for every row of one reply (enforced by the result's if/then); carried per row so rgb is checkable in place.

rgb.description: width x 3 bytes, pixels left to right, r,g,b per pixel — the S/H-applied output values (D9 category 1). This pattern is the whole-pixel floor; the exact per-mode length (1920 or 1536 hex digits) is enforced by the result's if/then.

rows.description: The requested rows, line-ascending, contiguous from startLine.

caveat.description: Present only when source is stateRender: no completed frame is retained — the machine has not completed one, or reset/reload_rom/restore dropped it — and the rows are rendered from VDP state as it stands now; mid-frame effects a real raster would show are NOT reproduced.

emulator/watchpoint_add.$comment: protocol.md §6 (breakpoints & watchpoints). Arms a RECORDING watch: it observes and does not halt unless `stopAfter` is given, in which case the run ends at the next instruction boundary and `emulator/stopped` fires with reason 'watchpoint' and a `watch` param naming the cause. Not subject to §6's run-control state rule — it mutates an observer, not the timeline. Refused with -32005 {reason:'watchCapReached'} at capabilities.watchpoints.maxWatches (D13 rule 3 applied to this surface).

space.description: Which address space. 'bus' is the 68000 address space (work RAM, ROM, Z80 RAM, I/O, VDP ports); the other three are VDP-INTERNAL byte-address spaces — the 'who wrote this tile / palette entry?' watch. Spaces never cross-trigger: a numeric collision between a bus address and a VRAM byte address matches only the watch in its own space.

addr.description: First address of the watched range, inclusive. D9 category 1.

symbol.description: Resolved to an address (D7); §4's round-trip rule binds it as it binds every method's `symbol` param. Valid ONLY with space 'bus' — a symbol names a 68000 address, and a VDP-internal byte address has no symbol. Any other space with `symbol` is -32602.

len.description: Length of the watched range in bytes; the range is addr..=addr+len-1. A count, so a JSON number (D9 category 2). Default 1 reproduces the single-address call this row carried before this amendment.

write.description: Match writes. Neither given means write-only: the recorded purpose of this instrument is 'who wrote this?'. Both true means any access. A write watch also matches the 68000 TAS (its read-modify-write store); a read watch does not.

mode.description: 'record' stores each matched access in the server's bounded hit ring. 'census' stores NOTHING and instead groups matched accesses by one key, which is what turns a watch over a wide range from a context bomb into a number. Both modes count `matched` either way.

censusKey.description: REQUIRED with mode 'census', and REFUSED (-32602) without it — a param this bus silently ignored would be a caller believing it asked for something it did not get, which §5's refuse-and-name ethos exists to prevent. 'value' is the distinct-value census: a WRITE COUNT IS A MISLEADING PROXY for how much a value moves, and this is the aggregate that survives that (protocol.md §6 prose). 'addr' answers which addresses in the range are actually touched. 'via' answers CPU-vs-DMA on a VDP-internal watch, which a function-code census cannot (there is no bus function code on a VDP-internal write).

stopAfter.description: Halt the run at the next instruction boundary once this watch has matched N accesses, emitting emulator/stopped with reason 'watchpoint'. ABSENT means the watch never affects when the machine stops. This is stop-on-condition, not an interactive break: the triggering instruction has fully committed when the run ends, and the run was already bounded by its own caller.

label.description: Optional human string, carried back verbatim and never interpreted.

allOf.$comment: §5's refuse-and-name ethos, enforced mechanically in both directions rather than left to prose: a `censusKey` without mode 'census' is -32602 and MUST NOT be silently ignored, and mode 'census' without a `censusKey` has no key to group by. D14 makes the schema the authority on which keys may appear together.

watch.description: The watch handle. Server-assigned, NEVER REUSED, and an opaque string per D9 category 4 — not an address and not an index. It cannot be an address: one address may carry several watches, and the same number names four different things across the four spaces. A client hands it back to watchpoint_clear and reads it off every hit.

op.description: The resolved op filter — what `read`/`write` actually became, so a caller that supplied neither is told what it got.

caveat.description: §2.4. Optional and handler-emitted; clients SHOULD surface it and MUST NOT parse it. Declared because §8 item 20 closes results against this fragment.

emulator/watchpoint_clear.$comment: protocol.md §6. The inverse of watchpoint_add, and the anti-staleness half of this surface: without it an armed watch outlives the session that wanted it. Idempotent — an unknown handle succeeds with removed: 0, per §6.1's rule for checkpoint_drop. Hits already recorded are NOT deleted; they keep naming their handle, and a handle absent from watchpoint_list is a retired watch.

caveat.description: §2.4. Optional, handler-emitted, never parsed.

emulator/watchpoint_list.$comment: protocol.md §6. The armed instrument, with what each watch has observed. §2.4's FLAT spelling of the bounded-list rule, used because the list here IS the whole result rather than a field of one: total/returned/limit/truncated as siblings of the array, the same field set as $defs/boundedList. A pure read: not subject to §6's run-control state rule. A handle that appears on a hit but not here is a watch that has been cleared — ids are never reused, so that test cannot give a false negative.

cursor.description: Continuation handle from a previous call. Opaque (D9 category 4); its behaviour is normative (protocol.md §2.4 clause (c)), its representation is the server's.

limit.description: House ceiling, the same 4096 read_memory and watchpoint_hits carry. A `limit` bounded on one list and unbounded on its sibling is two policies wearing one name.

stopAfter.description: Present only when this watch will halt the run. A watch left armed with this set is the one that can change a later capture's outcome, so it is listed rather than left to be discovered.

matched.description: Accesses this watch matched, counted in EVERY mode including the ones that store nothing. A count of writes, NOT a measure of how much the value changed — see the census below and protocol.md §6.

census.description: key -> count, ascending by key. Present only when mode is 'census'. The bounded group-by that makes a wide watch survivable, and — over censusKey 'value' — the aggregate that a raw write count misleads about.

key.description: The grouped value: an address, a written value, or 0=bus/1=direct(CPU)/2=dma for censusKey 'via'.

distinctKeys.description: How many distinct keys the census retained. A LOWER BOUND when keysCapped is true — never read distinctKeys == keyCap as an exact answer.

keyCap.description: The configured cap, so a reader can tell distinctKeys AT the cap from distinctKeys under it.

keysCapped.description: The census refused at least one new key because it was at its cap. Known keys keep counting past the cap; only new ones are refused. THE TYPED KEY, not a caveat: §2.4 rule 3 says any consequence a client must act on needs one.

censusOverflow.description: Accesses carrying a key the capped census could not retain. Counted, never silently dropped.

total.description: Watches armed in total, not on this page (§2.4 clause (a)).

returned.description: watches.length, restated so a client can compare it to `total` without counting.

limit.description: The page ceiling actually applied, which is not necessarily the one the client asked for (§2.4 clause (a), OPTIONAL).

cursor.description: Present when more remain. This method accepts a `cursor` param, so §2.4 clause (b) permits it to emit one.

caveat.description: §2.4. Optional, handler-emitted, never parsed.

emulator/watchpoint_hits.$comment: protocol.md §6. The recorded hit log — the 'who wrote this?' answer. POLLED, never pushed: a per-hit event would feed one bounded lossy stage (the ring) into another (the event queue), and moving droppedEvents for recorder volume would degrade the signal D17 defines for stopped/romReloaded. A pure read: not subject to §6's run-control state rule, and non-destructive, so two clients on one bus cannot steal each other's evidence. §2.4's flat bounded-list spelling, plus three counters that are NOT part of it: `dropped` (loss at record time), `seen` (the negative control) and `matched`.

watch.description: Return only hits recorded by this watch. Absent means every watch — the ring is one shared, seq-ordered stream.

cursor.description: Continuation handle. Opaque (D9 category 4). A hit dropped from the ring between two calls was not live at both requests, so resuming past it does not violate §2.4 clause (c)'s invariant; `dropped` moving is how a client learns it happened.

hits.description: Oldest first. Each hit is attributed to the instruction that drove it (pc, from the step boundary) and to the master that drove it (fc on the bus, via for a VDP-internal write).

watch.description: The watch that recorded this hit. REQUIRED: the ring is shared, so without it a log spanning two watches is uninterpretable — and a handle absent from watchpoint_list marks a hit recorded by a watch that has since been cleared, which is how a stale instrument's evidence stays distinguishable from a live one's.

value.description: The value read or written (for a VDP-internal write, the NEW value).

old.description: The value that was there before the access. Present IF AND ONLY IF space is not 'bus': the 68000 bus event stream carries no prior value, so a bus hit has none to report and emitting 0x0 would assert something false. Where present, old != value is the exact per-write change test — the measurement a raw write count misleads about.

size.description: Access width in bytes. A count (D9 category 2).

op.description: 'tas' is the 68000 read-modify-write store; it matches a write watch and not a read one.

fc.description: 68000 function code of the access (5/6 = CPU supervisor data/program, 0 = a non-CPU master). Present IF AND ONLY IF space is 'bus' — a VDP-internal write has no bus function code, and its CPU-vs-DMA attribution is `via`.

via.description: How the access reached its target. 'bus' = a 68000 bus access. 'direct' = a CPU data-port write into VDP memory; 'dma' = a DMA step, attributed to the instruction that TRIGGERED the transfer. This is the CPU-vs-DMA answer for VDP-internal writes, which no function code can give.

pc.description: PC of the instruction that drove the access, stamped at the step boundary. One instruction driving several accesses (a MOVEM, a read-modify-write) attributes them all to itself.

symbol.description: Nearest preceding label for `pc`, when symbols are loaded (D7). An annotation on the address, never a replacement for it. Typed as the round-trip name for §4's reason, the same retype §11.6 applied to read_memory's.

frame.description: Emulated frame of THIS HIT — deliberately inside the hit and never at the top level of the result, where the envelope stamp (§2.2) would overwrite it with the machine's current coordinate.

mclk.description: Emulated master clock of this hit. INSTRUCTION-GRANULAR whenever `space` is not 'bus' — a VDP-internal write is still drained after the driving CPU step, but it carries the clock the VDP performed the write at rather than borrowing that step's (corrected by §11.15). What remains is instruction granularity: the bus freezes its clock for one 68000 instruction, so a write is located to the start of the instruction that drove it, and every word of one DMA burst shares the transfer's instant. That bound is a standing property of a VDP hit and is stated in §6 rather than repeated as a per-reply caveat (§2.4's advisory: a caveat that is always present is one clients learn to ignore); narrowing it further is the registered follow-up F-SUBLINE-ACCESSMCLK.

seq.description: Monotonic id of the matched access, assigned in order and STABLE ACROSS RING DROPS — so a gap in seq marks hits the ring discarded. A count (D9 category 2); the cursor is the server's business and is not this number.

allOf.$comment: The two presence rules, enforced mechanically rather than left to prose. A bus hit has no prior value to report (the 68000 bus event stream carries none) and a VDP-internal write has no bus function code; emitting either as a zero would assert something false, which is the silent-wrong-answer class this bus exists to prevent. D14 makes the schema the authority on which keys exist, so the rule belongs here and not only in §6.

total.description: Hits the ring currently HOLDS that match this query — not `matched` (accesses, including ones no ring stored) and not `dropped` (hits the ring has already discarded). §2.4 clause (a)'s `total`, and the three numbers are deliberately distinct.

returned.description: hits.length, restated so a client can compare it to `total` without counting.

limit.description: The page ceiling actually applied, which is not necessarily the one the client asked for (§2.4 clause (a), OPTIONAL).

cursor.description: Present when more remain. This method accepts a `cursor` param, so §2.4 clause (b) permits it to emit one.

truncated.description: Loss at READ time — more hits are held than this page returned. Distinct from `dropped`. REQUIRED EVEN WHEN FALSE (§2.4 clause (a)).

dropped.description: Hits the recorder discarded at RECORD time because its ring was at capacity (oldest first). An INSTRUMENT fact, identical for every client — unlike droppedEvents (§2.3), which is a per-connection fact — which is why it rides in the body and not in the envelope. D17's principle, applied to the second lossy stage on this bus: a bounded ring that discards is correct, the silence is not.

seen.description: THE STRUCTURAL NEGATIVE CONTROL. Every access offered to the recorder, matched or not. seen > 0 with matched == 0 is a live instrument that found nothing; seen == 0 is an instrument that was never attached to the run, and a zero from it means nothing at all. REQUIRED so a client cannot mistake the second for the first — and REQUIRED as a typed number rather than carried in prose, per §2.4 rule 3.

matched.description: Accesses that matched at least one watch, across all modes. matched - total - dropped is what the non-recording watches absorbed. A count of accesses, not a measure of change.

caveat.description: §2.4: OPTIONAL, singular, handler-emitted, surfaced verbatim and never parsed. Every machine-actionable warning this instrument can raise already has a typed key — `seen`, `keysCapped`, `censusOverflow` — and the one permanent property (a VDP hit's step-granular `mclk`) is stated in §6 instead, because §2.4's advisory is that an always-present caveat is one clients learn to ignore.

emulator/set_profiler.$comment: protocol.md §6 (profiler), re-specified 2026-08-19 by §11.16 (CR-26) — an AMENDMENT to a row catalogued since this table's first draft, and the family's first fragment. Arms or disarms an exact per-invocation CPU-cycle accountant. Arming RESETS the accumulators (there is no resume in this revision, so a second arm discards an in-flight sample); disarming RETAINS the sample so it can still be read. The arm is SYNCHRONOUS with this reply — no sleep, no poll and no extra frame may be needed for it to take effect — and it MUST NOT be refused with -32005 for the machine's run state, because the sample's edges are frame boundaries and not the instant this command landed (a refusal about the INSTRUMENT's state, such as get_profiler_frames' perFrameNotArmed, is a different thing and is unaffected). The sample opens at the first frame boundary AFTER arming and closes at the most recent one, so a partial first frame is inexpressible. Prose-only, since JSON Schema cannot express them: the reset-on-arm, the retain-on-disarm and the boundary-delimited sample. AMENDED 2026-08-21 by §11.18 (CR-28), which adds the opt-in `callers` lens: a SECOND arming flag on the perFrame pattern, resetting with the rest of the accumulators on every arm, and echoed in the result by any server that implements it. Also prose-only: a server that omits limits.maxProfilerCallers has no lens, refuses the param as an undeclared key (§2.5), and omits the echo.

enabled.description: true arms the instrument (resetting it), false disarms it and retains what was accumulated. D9 category 2.

perFrame.description: OPT-IN per-frame recording, default false. When true the server also retains a bounded ring of whole-frame totals, readable as get_profiler_frames.perFrame; when false that key is absent from every reply and `frames` there is refused. Opt-in because a per-frame record costs memory across a long sample while the aggregate does not — the aggregate accumulates in place.

callers.description: OPT-IN per-caller accounting, default false (added 2026-08-21, §11.18). When true the server also accumulates, per routine, the call edges that reached it, readable as the `callers` list on each get_profiler_frames routine row; when false those keys are absent from every row and `topCallers` there is refused. Opt-in on the perFrame precedent and for the perFrame reason INVERTED: the accumulator cost is small — per-caller work is proportional to CALLS, not to instructions, because cycles are folded at invocation boundaries rather than keyed per step — but the REPLY grows by rows x edges, and this catalog's pattern is that a second lens is opt-in. A server that does not implement the lens omits limits.maxProfilerCallers and REFUSES this param with -32602 (§2.5); a server that does implement it MUST NOT refuse `callers:false`. That refusal is CAPABILITY-CONDITIONAL rather than a plain undeclared-key case, and §2.5 is being applied rather than analogized: it binds a server against the fragment AT THE REVISION IT IMPLEMENTS, and a lens a server does not implement is outside the surface it implements — so this key, though declared by the shared fragment post-amendment, is undeclared FOR THAT SERVER and refuses by name like any other.

enabled.description: The state the instrument is in after this call.

perFrame.description: Whether the per-frame ring is armed after this call. Echoed rather than assumed: it is the key that decides whether get_profiler_frames answers a `frames` param or refuses it.

callers.description: Whether per-caller accounting is armed after this call (added 2026-08-21, §11.18). Echoed for perFrame's reason: it is the key that decides whether get_profiler_frames answers a `topCallers` param or refuses it. REQUIRED of a server that advertises limits.maxProfilerCallers, and ABSENT from one that does not — a conditional this fragment cannot express in `required` without making every pre-§11.18 server non-conformant, which D5 bars now that a server ships this family (§11.16's pre-release window closed at the profiler arc's merge). Absence therefore means `this server has no caller lens`, never `the lens is off`; `false` means the lens exists and is off.

emulator/get_profiler.$comment: protocol.md §6 (profiler), re-specified 2026-08-19 by §11.16 (CR-26). The instrument's state, not its data — a pure read, never refused with -32005 for run state, and it clears nothing. framesRecorded is the SAME number get_profiler_frames reports as frameCount, and the two MUST agree when no frames were run between the calls: the legacy surface had two counts that could differ (one echoed the request, one counted pushes) and only one of them was ever the divisor. AMENDED 2026-08-21 by §11.18 (CR-28): the state this method reports gains `callers`, the third arming fact, on the same conditional-presence rule set_profiler's echo takes. No routine row appears here, so the caller LIST and its refusal belong entirely to get_profiler_frames.

enabled.description: Whether the instrument is armed right now.

perFrame.description: Whether the per-frame ring is armed.

callers.description: Whether per-caller accounting is armed (added 2026-08-21, §11.18). REQUIRED of a server that advertises limits.maxProfilerCallers and ABSENT from one that does not, for the reason set_profiler's echo carries it that way; absence means `no caller lens on this server`, `false` means `the lens exists and is off`. This method reports the instrument's STATE and never its data, so a routine row — and therefore a `callers` LIST — cannot appear here at all, and callersNotArmed is structurally unreachable on this method.

framesRecorded.description: Whole frames in the sample — COUNTED at each frame boundary observed while armed AFTER the one that opened the sample (that opening boundary is never counted, so n boundaries observed delimit n-1 whole frames), never derived by subtracting frame indices, which are positions on a clock `reset` restarts (§2.2). REQUIRED, not optional: 0 is a real answer (nothing recorded yet) and absence would be a second way to say it. Equals get_profiler_frames.frameCount.

routineCount.description: Distinct routine rows accumulated, before any `top` bound is applied — the same number get_profiler_frames reports as routines.total. A client can see the sample has content without asking for the content.

emulator/get_profiler_frames.$comment: protocol.md §6 (profiler), re-specified 2026-08-19 by §11.16 (CR-26). The accumulated sample: per-routine rows keyed by ENTRY ADDRESS, plus interrupt buckets keyed by CAUSE. A pure read — never refused with -32005 for run state, and it clears nothing, so two clients on one bus cannot consume each other's sample. DIVISION HAPPENS HERE: every row figure, both buckets and totalCycles are per-frame figures over the sample (the exact total divided by frameCount), with sampleCycles carrying the undivided whole-sample total and perFrameExact reporting whether any division truncated. Nothing is fabricated: no count is floored UP, no zero denominator is substituted, and an empty sample is frameCount 0 with empty lists rather than an error. Prose-only, since JSON Schema cannot express them: routines ordered by `cycles` descending; stallCycles <= cycles on every row; sampleCycles == frameCount * totalCycles exactly when perFrameExact is true; frameCount 0 implies every divided figure is 0 and perFrameExact is true; THE RECONCILIATION IDENTITY (added 2026-08-19 by §11.16's delta) — over the undivided sample, sum of routines' cyclesSelf + sum of interrupts' cyclesSelf + unattributedCycles == sampleCycles, exactly, which on the wire reconstructs as (that sum) * frameCount + unattributedCycles — every term of it a key of this reply, which is why cyclesSelf is REQUIRED on an interrupt bucket and not only on a row — and is GUARANTEED to close exactly when perFrameExact is true, may fall SHORT by at most frameCount-1 per summed figure when it is false and never over, and may still close exactly then, because that flag reports truncation in EVERY divided figure and not only in the ones this sum touches; calls counts COMPLETED invocations, so a routine still running at the close has a row carrying its accrued cycles with calls 0; and the caveat is emitted for abandonedFrames/depthExceeded only when one of them is non-zero, never constantly; and — added by the THIRD delta — each divided figure on a routine row or an interrupt bucket has an UNDIVIDED partner (cycles/cyclesTotal, cyclesSelf/cyclesSelfTotal, stallCycles/stallCyclesTotal, calls/callsTotal) with divided == total / frameCount under integer division when frameCount > 0, so divided * frameCount <= total < (divided + 1) * frameCount; the identity therefore ALSO holds over the undivided terms as sum(routines cyclesSelfTotal) + sum(interrupts cyclesSelfTotal) + unattributedCycles == sampleCycles, exactly and unconditionally, which is the form a client should check; and the four undivided fields are carried on the routine row and the interrupt bucket ONLY — never on perFrame[] rows, which are whole-frame totals with no per-routine breakdown and are already undivided. AMENDED 2026-08-21 by §11.18 (CR-28), which adds the OPT-IN per-caller breakdown: `topCallers` in the params, and four keys on the routine row (callers/callersTotal/callersReturned/callersTruncated) that arrive or stay away as a set, present iff the sample was armed with set_profiler{callers:true}. Prose-only, since JSON Schema cannot express them: each row's `callers` list is ordered by `cycles` descending; every invocation has exactly one caller edge, so when a row's callersTruncated is false its edges' callsTotal sum EXACTLY to the row's callsTotal and its edges' cyclesSelfTotal sum EXACTLY to the row's cyclesSelfTotal — both undivided on both sides, so both are == gates rather than bounds; the edge figures `cycles` and `cyclesSelf` are DIVIDED like every other divided figure here, so perFrameExact ranges over them and an armed caller lens can turn a reply's perFrameExact from true to false without anything being wrong; and the aggregate figures, the identity and every existing row key are UNMOVED by arming the lens — a client that never arms it sees a byte-identical reply.

frames.description: Bound on the per-frame list only: return at most this many of the most recent per-frame rows. It does NOT select the aggregate window — the aggregate is always the whole sample, which is what retires the legacy divisor-by-request-window. REFUSED with -32005 (data.reason = 'perFrameNotArmed') when the sample was not armed with set_profiler{perFrame:true}, because a parameter that cannot affect the answer is worse than one that is rejected. Above maxProfilerFrames it is refused with -32602, never clamped.

top.description: Bound on routines.items — the N most expensive rows by `cycles`. Above the server's advertised maxProfilerRoutines it is REFUSED with -32602, never silently clamped to the cap (the legacy surface clamped, so a caller could not tell a full list from a clipped one). D9 category 2.

topCallers.description: Added 2026-08-21, §11.18. Bound on each routine row's `callers` list — the N most expensive edges by `cycles`, per row, independently. It does NOT gate whether the lists appear: presence is decided by the ARM (set_profiler{callers:true}), exactly as the per-frame list's presence is, and this param only narrows what an armed reply carries. Above the server's advertised maxProfilerCallers it is REFUSED with -32602, never clamped (the `top` precedent). REFUSED with -32005 (data.reason = 'callersNotArmed') when the sample was not armed for callers, because a parameter that cannot affect the answer is worse than one that is rejected — the `frames`/perFrameNotArmed rule with the lens changed and nothing else. D9 category 2.

frameCount.description: Whole frames in the sample, counted at each boundary observed while armed AFTER the one that opened the sample (n boundaries observed delimit n-1 whole frames) — the divisor every per-frame figure in this reply was produced with. Read it; do not assume it equals the frames you ran, since that depends on where in the frame the instrument was armed. Equals get_profiler.framesRecorded.

sampleCycles.description: The UNDIVIDED total: CPU cycles the machine retired across the whole sample. Exact, always. When perFrameExact is true this equals frameCount * totalCycles, which is what lets a client recover every row's exact total by multiplication instead of being handed both.

totalCycles.description: CPU cycles the machine retired in ONE frame of the sample — sampleCycles divided by frameCount. The denominator a share is taken against, and the numerator budgetPct is derived from. Not the sum of the routine rows: rows are inclusive of callees, so they sum past it by construction.

unattributedCycles.description: Added 2026-08-19 by §11.16's delta. UNDIVIDED cycles the sample retired that belong to no row and no bucket, and the term that keeps the reconciliation identity closed: sum of routines' cyclesSelf + sum of interrupts' cyclesSelf + this == sampleCycles, over the undivided sample, exactly. Exactly one source: the in-sample time of an interrupt already in flight when the sample opened, whose bucket may not be opened retroactively (§6). Those cycles are real and are inside sampleCycles, so reporting them is what prevents a silent shortfall. Normally 0; non-zero is the ordinary phase for a ROM whose VBlank handler straddles the opening boundary, so it is information rather than an alarm. REQUIRED even when 0.

abandonedFrames.description: Added 2026-08-19 by §11.16's delta. UNDIVIDED count of frames torn off the shadow stack without completing — a routine an RTE unwound past, or one displaced by a stack the server could not follow. Their CYCLES are still reported (they ran); their CALLS are not (they never finished), so non-zero means some row's calls understates its invocations. A fact about the MEASUREMENT rather than about the program, typed rather than left to prose because a client reconciling rows wants it machine-readable. REQUIRED even when 0 (§2.3's reason: absence and zero must not both mean 'nothing happened'), and the conditional caveat mentions it only when non-zero.

depthExceeded.description: Added 2026-08-19 by §11.16's delta. UNDIVIDED count of calls the server declined to track because its shadow stack was already at its bound. Their cycles are charged to the innermost tracked frame, so nothing leaves the totals and the identity still closes — but those routines get no rows of their own and the frame they charge to is overstated. Non-zero means the server lost the thread of the program's stack: a measurement fact, reported rather than inferred from rows that do not add up. REQUIRED even when 0; the conditional caveat mentions it only when non-zero.

perFrameExact.description: TYPED, not a caveat (§2.4 rule 3), and REQUIRED even when true. True iff EVERY divided figure in this reply divided without remainder. When false, each divided figure is floored — one-sided low, bounded by one unit per figure — and a client gating with == must act on that. It is also what makes `cycles - stallCycles` exact arithmetic rather than the difference of two truncations, which is the subtraction the ideal-cycle gates on the other side of this bus are built on. With frameCount 0 there was nothing to divide, so it is true.

budgetPct.description: totalCycles as a percentage of one frame's CPU-cycle budget, DERIVED from the timingBasis this same server advertises (§2.1, D16) — mclkPerFrame over the master clocks per CPU cycle — never a hardcoded constant, which is wrong by ~16% the moment the machine is PAL. A sanity check on the accounting rather than a measure of load: on a machine whose CPU is never halted it sits near 100. Present unless budgetPctOmitted is.

budgetPctOmitted.description: Present INSTEAD of budgetPct when the derivation is ambiguous, naming the condition rather than averaging over it: the machine's timing basis changed inside the sample, so no single frame budget describes it. Exactly one of budgetPct / budgetPctOmitted is present, enforced by the result's anyOf + not.

routines.$comment: §2.4's NESTED container spelling, because this list is a FIELD of a larger result rather than the whole of it (the flat spelling belongs to emulator/checkpoint_list, whose result IS its list). A POLICY bound — the server picks the cap, `top` is the client's hint — so total/returned/truncated are mandatory and truncated is required even when false. NO cursor: this method accepts no continuation param, and §2.4 clause (b) forbids emitting a token that can never be handed back.

addr.description: The routine's ENTRY address, masked to the 24 address lines the 68000 drives, so a row key and a listing address compare directly instead of through a client-side mask. The row's identity: rows are keyed by entry address, never by symbol.

name.description: The BARE label at `addr` — §4's naming rule, which binds every symbol field on this bus. Never a `name+$hex` composite: the displacement is `disp`, and a rendering like 'Parallax_Update+$1A' is the two fields concatenated by a client that wants it. Absent, together with `disp`, when nothing resolves — a server MUST NOT fall back to the address string, because a client cannot tell a symbol spelled like an address from a lookup that failed.

disp.description: Bytes past `name`; 0 is an exact hit, which is the normal case here because a row key IS an entry address. Travels with `name` in both directions (dependentRequired).

cycles.description: Per-frame CPU cycles attributed to this routine, INCLUSIVE of everything it called — the meaning the legacy rows had in practice, kept so a migrating consumer's arithmetic does not change. Inclusive rows sum past totalCycles by construction; that is not an error, it is what inclusive means.

cyclesSelf.description: The same span with callee time subtracted — the additive half of the pair, and the one that sums to at most totalCycles across all rows. A client wanting a share of frame time divides THIS by totalCycles; the legacy `pct` divided the inclusive figure and summed far past 100%, which is why no pct key is emitted here.

stallCycles.description: The part of `cycles` the CPU spent held off the bus rather than executing — a SUBSET of `cycles`, keyed identically to it (same routine key, same inclusive span, same in-server division), so `cycles - stallCycles` is a well-formed subtraction rather than two quantities with different aggregation glued together. Exactly three conditions count, enumerated so that a fourth is a visible amendment and never a silent widening: a 68000 write to the VDP data port held off while the write FIFO is full; a 68000 read of that port waiting for the FIFO to drain; and the whole bus-hold window of a 68k->VDP DMA, billed to the instruction that armed it. A VRAM fill and a VRAM copy contribute nothing (the 68000 keeps running through both).

calls.description: Per-frame invocations of this routine — a COUNT, never floored up. A routine invoked fewer times than the sample has frames reports 0 here; the legacy surface substituted 1, which fabricated a call that never happened. It is the consumer's free correctness check: a fixture that failed to install shows the wrong count before any cycle figure is read.

cyclesTotal.description: Added 2026-08-19 by §11.16's third delta. UNDIVIDED over the whole sample — cycles BEFORE the division, not a second measurement of it: when frameCount > 0, cycles == cyclesTotal / frameCount under integer division, so this figure also BOUNDS its partner's truncation (cycles * frameCount <= cyclesTotal < (cycles + 1) * frameCount). Exact regardless of perFrameExact. Inclusive of everything this routine called, like its partner.

cyclesSelfTotal.description: Added 2026-08-19 by §11.16's third delta. UNDIVIDED over the whole sample — cyclesSelf BEFORE the division, not a second measurement of it: when frameCount > 0, cyclesSelf == cyclesSelfTotal / frameCount under integer division, so this figure also BOUNDS its partner's truncation (cyclesSelf * frameCount <= cyclesSelfTotal < (cyclesSelf + 1) * frameCount). Exact regardless of perFrameExact. THE IDENTITY'S WIRE TERM: sum of routines' cyclesSelfTotal + sum of interrupts' cyclesSelfTotal + unattributedCycles == sampleCycles, exactly, with no perFrameExact condition and no floor bound — which is why this field is REQUIRED rather than merely convenient, and why it is carried on the bucket as well as on the row.

stallCyclesTotal.description: Added 2026-08-19 by §11.16's third delta. UNDIVIDED over the whole sample — stallCycles BEFORE the division, not a second measurement of it: when frameCount > 0, stallCycles == stallCyclesTotal / frameCount under integer division, so this figure also BOUNDS its partner's truncation (stallCycles * frameCount <= stallCyclesTotal < (stallCycles + 1) * frameCount). Exact regardless of perFrameExact. Still a subset of cyclesTotal on the same routine, so cyclesTotal - stallCyclesTotal is the ideal-cycle figure with no truncation in either term.

callsTotal.description: Added 2026-08-19 by §11.16's third delta. UNDIVIDED over the whole sample — calls BEFORE the division, not a second measurement of it: when frameCount > 0, calls == callsTotal / frameCount under integer division, so this figure also BOUNDS its partner's truncation (calls * frameCount <= callsTotal < (calls + 1) * frameCount). Exact regardless of perFrameExact. REQUIRED because a per-frame count is the one figure here that division routinely DESTROYS rather than merely truncates: a routine invoked 4.53 times per frame reports calls 2, and one invoked once across the sample reports calls 0 — both correct, since a count is never floored up, and neither equality-gatable against a fire count derived from engine source. Counts COMPLETED invocations on the same rule calls uses, so a routine still running at the close carries its cycles with callsTotal 0, and abandonedFrames is where that understatement is reported.

callers.description: Added 2026-08-21, §11.18. OPT-IN per-caller breakdown of THIS row: one entry per distinct call edge that reached this routine, ordered by `cycles` DESCENDING so a bounded list is the expensive end rather than an arbitrary slice — the rule routines.items already carries, applied one level down. Present if and only if the sample was armed with set_profiler{callers:true}; `topCallers` narrows an armed list and never conjures one. Bounded by maxProfilerCallers, a POLICY bound, so §2.4 clause (a)'s three companions ride beside it as row siblings (callersTotal / callersReturned / callersTruncated) rather than as a nested {items,...} container — §2.4's FLAT spelling scoped to an ITEM, which that section's own selection rule now names for this case (widened by §11.18, with this list as the registered case) rather than leaving §6 to ship one form while §2.4 instructs another. NO cursor: this method accepts no continuation param and §2.4 clause (b) forbids emitting a token that can never be handed back. No per-row `limit` sibling either: the applied ceiling is one number for the entire reply (the client's topCallers, or the advertised cap), so repeating it on every row would be a constant field wearing signal's clothes — §2.4's constant-caveat advisory in field form — and §2.4 makes `limit` OPTIONAL.

callerAddr.description: ENTRY address of the routine that made these calls, masked to the 24 address lines the 68000 drives — the same key space the row's own `addr` uses, so an edge joins to its caller's row by string equality and needs no client-side mask. ABSENT when the edge has no calling routine address to name, and its absence is never a fabricated 0x0: the three ways that happens are enumerated by `entryKind`, which is REQUIRED exactly then. ONE CAVEAT A CLIENT MUST NOT ASSUME AWAY: when the calling frame is the sample's INFERRED ROOT — the frame the accountant opened on whatever PC retired first, having started mid-program — this address is real and is where the call came from, but it is NOT an entry point, so it may resolve to a bare label at a NON-ZERO callerDisp or to nothing at all. A client that assumes every callerAddr is a routine entry will mis-render exactly one edge per sample.

callerName.description: The BARE label at callerAddr — §4's naming rule, which binds every symbol field on this bus. Never a `name+$hex` composite: the displacement is callerDisp, and the concatenation is the client's to render. Absent, together with callerDisp, when nothing resolves — a server MUST NOT fall back to the address string, for the row field's reason: a client cannot tell a symbol spelled like an address from a lookup that failed. Requires callerAddr, since a name with no address to name is not a fact about anything.

callerDisp.description: Bytes past callerName. 0 is the normal case here exactly as on the row, because a call edge is keyed by the caller's ENTRY address — but unlike the row there is one SYSTEMATIC exception a client must expect rather than treat as a lookup failure: the inferred-root caller is keyed mid-routine and carries a non-zero displacement (see callerAddr). Travels with callerName in both directions (dependentRequired).

entryKind.description: Added 2026-08-21, §11.18. REQUIRED exactly when callerAddr is absent, and forbidden when it is present — enforced mechanically by this shape's if/then/else rather than left to this sentence. It exists because ONE ABSENCE WOULD OTHERWISE MEAN SEVERAL DIFFERENT FACTS: `hint` — the routine was entered from within a level-4 (HBlank) interrupt's context, so its caller is that BUCKET and there is no calling routine address to give; `vint` — the same, from the level-6 (VBlank) bucket; `root` — this row's routine IS the frame the sample opened on, so no call into it was ever observed; `depthCap` — the calling frame was one the accountant declined to track because its shadow stack was at its bound, which is the same event `depthExceeded` counts in the aggregate. A fabricated 0x0 in place of any of them is barred. THE INTERRUPT CASE IS SPLIT BY CAUSE, not carried as one `interrupt` value, and that is this family's own rule reaching one level down: §6 keys interrupt accounting by CAUSE and never collapses hint and vint anywhere else, so a single collapsing value would be the one place in this surface where the two are indistinguishable — and these two values JOIN the edge to the bucket it came from BY NAME, which a collapsing value cannot do. It is also the one spelling decision that could not be deferred: widening an emitted enum later is NOT additive, since a client or vendored validator closed over the old value set refuses the new member. Note the two senses of ROOT that meet on this shape and are NOT the same fact: `entryKind: 'root'` says THIS ROW had no observed caller, while the inferred-root caveat on callerAddr describes an edge that DOES carry an address which happens to be mid-routine.

cycles.description: Per-frame CPU cycles this routine accrued when reached from THIS caller, INCLUSIVE of everything it called — the row's own `cycles`, partitioned by caller. Divided by the same frameCount as every other divided figure in this reply, so perFrameExact ranges over these too: arming the caller lens ADDS divided figures, and a reply that would have been exact without it may report false with it. Inclusive figures double-count by construction, so a client checking that the edges account for the row should sum cyclesSelfTotal (below) and not this.

cyclesSelf.description: The same span with callee time subtracted — callee self-time attributed by caller, which is the figure the requesting consumer named as the one they came for. Per-frame, divided by frameCount; its undivided partner is cyclesSelfTotal, which is the term a client should actually reconcile with.

calls.description: Per-frame invocations of this routine made from this caller — a COUNT, never floored up, so an edge exercised fewer times than the sample has frames reports 0 here and the exact number is callsTotal. Counts COMPLETED invocations, on the row field's rule.

cyclesTotal.description: Added 2026-08-21, §11.18 (folded in at adjudication). UNDIVIDED inclusive cycles over the whole sample from this caller — cycles BEFORE the division, not a second measurement of it: when frameCount > 0, cycles == cyclesTotal / frameCount under integer division, so this figure also BOUNDS its partner's truncation. Exact regardless of perFrameExact. Inclusive figures double-count by construction, so this is NOT the term to sum against the row; cyclesSelfTotal is.

cyclesSelfTotal.description: Added 2026-08-21, §11.18 (folded in at adjudication). UNDIVIDED self cycles over the whole sample from this caller — cyclesSelf BEFORE the division, exact regardless of perFrameExact, bounding its partner's truncation the same way. NORMATIVE SUM: every invocation of a routine has exactly one caller edge, so when callersTruncated is false the edges' cyclesSelfTotal sum to the ROW's cyclesSelfTotal EXACTLY, with no floor slack in either term. It is required for the reason the row's own partner is required (§11.16's third delta) and one the delta could not have anticipated: without it this partition would be a normative sum no suite gate could assert with ==, which is §11.16's own QUIET GAP reproduced one level down — a shortfall of at most frameCount-1 per summed figure reads exactly like agreement.

callsTotal.description: UNDIVIDED invocations over the whole sample from this caller — calls BEFORE the division, exact regardless of perFrameExact, and the LOUD half of the same pair: a per-frame count is the one figure division routinely DESTROYS rather than merely truncates (§11.16's third delta), and an edge is a smaller denominator than a row, so it destroys counts MORE often, not less. NORMATIVE SUM: when callersTruncated is false, the edges' callsTotal sum to the row's callsTotal exactly.

items.description: ONE call-edge shape. Symmetric with the routine row wherever the two describe the same quantity, deliberately: an asymmetric tuple invites the mis-read this catalog warns about elsewhere. Every divided figure it carries has its undivided partner beside it (cycles/cyclesTotal, cyclesSelf/cyclesSelfTotal, calls/callsTotal), which is the routine row's own discipline at a smaller denominator. It carries no stallCycles — the requesting consumer DECLINED a per-edge stall figure on measured grounds (flat and VBlank-owned at every state they took), so its absence is a demand-side decision rather than an oversight, and the closure below bars the key rather than merely omitting it.

callersTotal.description: Added 2026-08-21, §11.18. Distinct call edges observed for this routine, BEFORE maxProfilerCallers or topCallers bounded the list — §2.4 clause (a)'s `total`. The cap is a REPLY bound and not a retention bound, which is what makes this number the true count of callers rather than the count that survived a ceiling. 0 IS THE TYPE'S FLOOR AND NOT AN EXPECTED READING: under this contract every row that exists acquired at least one edge — called gives the caller's edge, an unobserved caller gives `root`, a lost frame gives `depthCap`, an interrupt context gives the cause edge — so an implementer meeting an armed row with an empty edge list should treat it as a defect in the accountant rather than as an ordinary answer.

callersReturned.description: Added 2026-08-21, §11.18. §2.4 clause (a)'s `returned`: the length of `callers`, restated so a client can compare it against callersTotal without walking the array and so the three numbers are checkable against each other rather than individually plausible.

callersTruncated.description: Added 2026-08-21, §11.18. §2.4 clause (a)'s `truncated`, and REQUIRED even when false — absence and false must not both mean `you have every caller` (§2.3's reason). It is also the guard on both normative edge-versus-row sums: they hold when this is false and are lower bounds when it is true. Per-row rather than per-reply, because one reply legitimately carries some rows complete and others clipped: the bound is applied to each row's edge list independently.

items.description: ONE row shape. Ordered by `cycles` descending, so a truncated list is the expensive end rather than an arbitrary slice. The four `callers*` keys are OPT-IN and arrive or stay away as a SET — all four present when the sample was armed with set_profiler{callers:true}, all four absent otherwise, tied mechanically by dependentRequired so a half-served lens cannot pass this fragment.

interrupts.$comment: Keyed by interrupt CAUSE — hint is level 4 (HBlank), vint is level 6 (VBlank) — and never by handler address. The legacy instrument classified on the handler's entry PC tested against vector-table constants, so on a ROM whose handlers live anywhere else `hint` was HBlank PLUS VBlank and `vint` was structurally 0: a silently wrong number rather than a missing one. Both buckets are always present, including when a run took neither interrupt, so a zero means 'measured zero' and not 'not reported'.

perFrame.$comment: OPT-IN: present if and only if the sample was armed with set_profiler{perFrame:true}. Whole-frame totals only — no per-routine breakdown — and NOT divided, since a per-frame row is already per frame. Bounded by maxProfilerFrames (a policy bound, so total/returned/truncated are mandatory) and by the `frames` param; no cursor, per §2.4 clause (b). This is what makes the method's name true: the legacy get_profiler_frames returned one averaged object and no way to see variance within a sample at all.

frame.description: The machine's own frame index at this row's closing boundary — the same coordinate §2.2 stamps. A position on a clock `reset` restarts, so a client CORRELATES with it and does not subtract two of them to count frames; frameCount is the count.

cycles.description: CPU cycles the machine retired in this one frame. Undivided — there is nothing to divide.

stallCycles.description: Of those cycles, the ones spent held off the bus — the same three conditions the row field enumerates.

hintCycles.description: Cycles this frame's level-4 (HBlank) interrupts cost, inclusive of everything their handlers called.

vintCycles.description: Cycles this frame's level-6 (VBlank) interrupt cost, inclusive of everything its handler called.

caveat.description: §2.4: OPTIONAL, singular, handler-emitted, surfaced verbatim and never parsed. CONDITIONAL, as §2.4's advisory requires — an empty sample is the case it exists for. Every machine-actionable consequence here already has a typed key (perFrameExact, budgetPctOmitted, truncated), and declaring the field is §2.4 rule 4, not an intention to emit it on every reply.

cycles.description: Per-frame cycles this bucket cost, INCLUSIVE of everything the handler called — entry, the handler, its callees and the RTE. The bucket opens when the interrupt is TAKEN (the acknowledge cycle, not the raise) and closes at the matching RTE — the one that unwinds that interrupt's own exception frame, so the RTE of an exception taken INSIDE the handler (a TRAP, an address error) closes that exception and not the bucket, and an RTE that finds no open bucket closes nothing. An interrupt taken before the sample opened accrues to no bucket: a server MUST NOT retroactively open one. Nesting is by depth and never double-counted: cycles retired while a nested HBlank runs inside a VBlank handler belong to hint alone, and the suspended vint bucket accrues nothing until the nested one closes.

cyclesSelf.description: Added 2026-08-19 by §11.16's delta ruling. The bucket's cycles with the time of everything it called subtracted — the same self/inclusive pair a routine row carries, keyed identically to `cycles` and divided by the same frameCount, so the two are summable. REQUIRED because the reconciliation identity sums it: an interrupt handler's own code gets a routines[] row of its own, so the bucket's SELF figure is the interrupt cost that belongs to no row (entry, the span before the handler's first instruction, and the RTE). Without it on the wire the identity in §6 would name a term no client could read, which is the defect the delta ruling caught.

stallCycles.description: Of those cycles, the ones spent held off the bus — same definition, same keying and same division as the routine row's field, so the same subtraction works here.

calls.description: Per-frame times this interrupt was TAKEN, not the times it was raised: a raised-but-masked HBlank appears nowhere in this reply. A count, never floored up.

Exact regardless of perFrameExact. Inclusive of everything this bucket called, like its partner.

Exact regardless of perFrameExact. Still a subset of cyclesTotal on the same bucket, so cyclesTotal - stallCyclesTotal is the ideal-cycle figure with no truncation in either term.

count.description: Instructions to step. ≥1, default 1, ≤1000000; a value outside is REFUSED with -32602, never clamped (protocol.md §6, §11.24, closing audit D-02). Zero was refused rather than clamped because the two servers disagreed on it and a step of nothing is a status call spelt wrong.

pc.description: Program counter after the step. D9 category 1.

symbol.$comment: The BARE label at `pc` — §4's naming rule, which binds every symbol field on this bus. Absent when nothing resolves; a server MUST NOT fall back to the address string.

symbolDisp.description: Bytes past `symbol`; 0 is an exact hit. Non-negative because it is a displacement from the NEAREST PRECEDING symbol (§4).

stepped.description: Instructions actually retired by this call. Minimum 0, not 1 (corrected 2026-09-04, oracle finding on serving 11.33): a CPU already halted on STOP retires nothing, and absence means the count ran, so 0 is the only legal spelling of that state. Added 2026-09-04 (protocol.md section 11.33, oracle CR-STEP-SHORTFALL): a server that bounds a step inside a frame budget stops early when count is too large to retire inside it, and until this key the reply had no way to say so (no reached, and caveat is declared ABSENT on this row), so a caller read count instructions as having run. Equal to count when the step completed; LESS than count when the bound stopped it, and then the machine is wherever the bound left it, NOT count instructions on. A server that bounds steps MUST emit it whenever stepped < count and SHOULD emit it always; a server that never bounds may omit it, and absence means the count ran, never a shortfall. Never greater than count (not expressible here across params and result; the gate cannot check it, the server must). The stopped event's deadlineReached carries the same fact on the event channel; this is the reply-side spelling, so a caller that never listens to events still sees it.

emulator/run_to_scanline.$comment: protocol.md §6 (run-control) and D12, row at §6 line 855: `line (0–511), maxFrames? (≥1, def 600) | line, reached, maxFrames, caveat?`. FIRST FRAGMENT, transcribed 2026-08-22. The emulator/run_to fragment is the direct precedent and this row is its sibling: bounded, and it says whether it fired. Named in §6's run-control state rule, so it requires a PAUSED machine and MUST fail -32005 machineRunning otherwise. `reached` is the caller's answer and `deadlineReached` on the `stopped` event is its complement for stream consumers; they are never both true (§6). caveat is DECLARED here, unlike most rows, because §6's row spells it out and D12 gives it SHOULD force: a `reached: false` reply SHOULD say in words that nothing about the machine's state follows from where it stopped. line.description: Target scanline. D9 category 2 (a line number). The 0–511 span is §6's and deliberately wider than emulator/scanlines' 0–223 active-display bound: a raster target may legitimately sit in blanking, which is not a drawable row.

maxFrames.description: Bound (D12). Without it an unreachable line is an unbounded run, and a hang in the debug transport destroys evidence.

reached.description: True = the condition fired. False = the run ended on maxFrames; NOTHING about the machine state follows from where it stopped (D12).

caveat.description: §2.4. SHOULD be present when `reached` is false — the one discharge D12 asks for in words. §2.4 clause 4 exempts most rows from enumerating caveat; this row is one of the two that keep it explicitly (run_to being the other), because here it is a specific obligation and not a general warning.

emulator/wait_for_break.$comment: protocol.md §6 (run-control), row at §6 line 857: `timeoutMs? | running, pc?, symbol?, timeoutReached?, waitedMs?`. FIRST FRAGMENT, transcribed 2026-08-22. DEPRECATED by the emulator/stopped event (§3, §8 item 9, D6) and RETAINED for one transition window: clients without the `events` capability may still poll it, and a server MUST keep answering it. `running` is NOT declared here — it is the machine stamp's (§2.2, D11), applied envelope-level after the handler returns and arriving through replyFields; §6's row lists it because the row predates D11, and declaring it twice would invite a handler to think it owns the value. That is emulator/status's ruling applied to the second row that repeats a stamp field, (§6 struck it 2026-08-26 by §11.24, closing D-05). THE ROW HAS NO REQUIRED HANDLER KEY: every one of the remaining four is optional in §6, so a conformant reply can be the envelope alone. §5 spells this method's flag `timeout_reached` while §6 spells it `timeoutReached`; §3's camelCase-fields convention makes §6's the one true spelling and §5's a stale snake_case survival — §5 corrected 2026-08-26 by §11.24 (D-06 closed). caveat is declared ABSENT: `timeoutReached` is the typed key §2.4 rule 3 asks for, so the weak answer here already has a machine-readable discriminant.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait, ms. Default 30000 (the legacy server's measured default, preserved because a retained deprecated method keeps its behaviour); ≤300000, REFUSED above; 0 polls once and returns (protocol.md §6, §11.24, audit D-07 closed).

pc.description: Program counter where the machine stopped. Optional in §6's row: absent when the wait timed out with the machine still running.

symbol.description: The BARE label at `pc` (§4); `symbolDisp` carries the displacement.

timeoutReached.description: Whether the wait ended on its timeout rather than on a halt. The typed discriminant §2.4 rule 3 requires for a consequence a client acts on. §5 calls this field `timeout_reached`; §3's camelCase convention makes THIS the spelling (audit D-06).

waitedMs.description: Wall-clock milliseconds actually waited. The one wall-clock quantity in this catalog, and legitimately so: it measures the WAIT, which is a host-side fact, not a machine coordinate — D11's emulated-clocks rule governs the stamp beside it, not this.

symbolDisp.description: Bytes past `symbol`; 0 is an exact hit (§4). Added 2026-08-26 by §11.24 (audit D-08).

emulator/z80_read.$comment: protocol.md §6 (memory & Z80), row at §6 line 996: `addr (0–$3FFF), len? (≤$2000) | addr, len, bytes`. FIRST FRAGMENT, transcribed 2026-08-22. The Z80's address space is deliberately NOT a member of emulator/read's `space` enum (§6's read note is explicit: 'a read enum holding a value the watch enum refuses would be two vocabularies wearing one name'), so this row keeps its own bounds. Those bounds are stated on a HEX STRING and so cannot be expressed as minimum/maximum — the emulator/read precedent, which likewise carries its space sizes in prose — and live in the descriptions below. A pure read by the same reasoning that exempts emulator/read: it advances nothing, so §6's run-control state rule does not reach it. `len` defaults to 1 and over-ceiling is refused (§11.24, D-09 closed). caveat is declared ABSENT (the sprites precedent).

addr.description: First byte to read in the Z80's 16-bit space. §6 bounds it to 0–0x3FFF (the 8 KB of Z80 RAM); a base outside that is a refusal, not a wrap. D9 category 1, so the bound is prose here rather than a numeric maximum.

len.description: Bytes to read. Default 1; ceiling 0x2000 (8192). Above the ceiling, or addr+len past 0x4000, the request is REFUSED whole with -32004 (the range code every other address-ranged row uses; §11.28 aligned it from §11.22's -32602), never clamped — §11.22's z80_write rule applied to its read sibling (protocol.md §6, §11.24, audit D-09 closed).

emulator/z80_write.$comment: protocol.md §6 (memory & Z80), row at §6 line 1001: `addr (0–$3FFF); bytes|value (0–255) | addr, len`. Amended by §11.22 (audit D-10): `value` is EXACTLY ONE BYTE, 0–255, refused with -32602 outside that range and never masked; multi-byte writes use `bytes`, written low-address-first (the Z80 has no word order to get wrong at the bus, so no `width` machinery and no little-endian exception exist here — the row deliberately does NOT mirror write_memory). `addr` is bounded 0–0x3FFF and `addr + len` MUST NOT exceed 0x4000: an overrun is refused whole before any byte lands, never truncated or wrapped. The exactly-one-payload-spelling shape is write_memory's and is enforced mechanically (both, or neither, is -32602). Named in §6's run-control state rule by §11.22 (audit D-11): a poke mid-free-run mutates the timeline. caveat is declared ABSENT (the write_memory precedent).

addr.description: First byte to write in the Z80's space, 0–0x3FFF (§11.22). D9 category 1: the bound is prose here. `addr + len` above 0x4000 is refused whole with -32602.

bytes.description: Hex string of bytes written low-address-first starting at `addr` (§11.22). Even digit count; `addr + len` ≤ 0x4000.

value.description: Exactly one byte (§11.22). Out of range is -32602, never masked to eight bits. For more than one byte use `bytes`.

len.description: Bytes written. Determinate for a `bytes` payload; underdetermined for a `value` one until §6 pins a width (audit D-10).

emulator/audio_spectrum.$comment: protocol.md §6 (audio / VGM), row at §6 line 1388: `source? (fm|psg, def fm), fftSize? (256–32768, def 4096, →pow2), maxHz? | source, sampleRate, fftSize, binHz, dominantHz, samplesAvailable, magnitudes[]`. FIRST FRAGMENT, transcribed 2026-08-22. The row is unusually complete for an unschematized one: both param enums, the range and the default are all spelled out. ONE READING IS APPLIED AND FLAGGED: the row's '→pow2' annotation is read as the server COERCING the request to a power of two, so the RESULT's fftSize is enumerated over the eight powers of two in 256–32768 while the PARAM accepts the whole range — which is why the two are typed differently on purpose. §6 does not say whether the coercion rounds up, down or to nearest, and it need not for this enum to hold. `magnitudes` is STRUCTURALLY bounded (its length follows from the echoed fftSize, narrowed by maxHz), so per §2.4 clause (d) it takes neither a truncation flag nor a cursor — pixel_attribution's `candidates` is the exemplar. A pure read: it reads an audio buffer and advances nothing, so §6's run-control state rule does not reach it. WHAT §6 DOES NOT SAY, all registered as audit D-22: `maxHz` is not echoed although it determines the array's length; `magnitudes`' UNIT is unstated (linear amplitude or decibels), which two conformant servers can answer differently with identically-shaped replies; and `samplesAvailable` below fftSize has no stated consequence. caveat is declared ABSENT because §6's row declares none — but `samplesAvailable` under `fftSize` is exactly the weaker-answer condition §2.4 exists for, which is part of D-22.

source.description: Which chip's output to analyse. An unknown value is -32602.

fftSize.description: Requested transform size. §6 accepts the whole 256–32768 range and marks the field '→pow2', so a non-power-of-two request is COERCED rather than refused; the reply's `fftSize` is the size actually used. D9 category 2.

maxHz.description: Ceiling on the frequency range returned, narrowing `magnitudes` to the bins at or below it. NOT echoed in the reply, though it determines the array's length — audit D-22.

source.description: Echoed, so a reply is self-describing: a spectrum means nothing without the chip it came from.

sampleRate.description: Sample rate of the analysed buffer, in Hz. The basis binHz is derived from.

fftSize.description: The transform size ACTUALLY used, which is the request coerced to a power of two ('→pow2' in §6's row) and so is one of the eight powers of two inside 256–32768. Enumerated rather than left an open integer because a client sizing its own arithmetic off this number needs the coercion's result, not its request.

binHz.description: Width of one bin in Hz — sampleRate over fftSize. Fractional by construction, hence a JSON number.

dominantHz.description: Centre frequency of the largest-magnitude bin, in Hz.

samplesAvailable.description: How many samples the analysed buffer actually held. The honesty field of this row: below `fftSize` the transform was taken over a short buffer, and §6 states no consequence for that — audit D-22.

magnitudes.description: Per-bin magnitudes, bin-ascending from DC. STRUCTURALLY bounded — the length follows from the echoed fftSize, narrowed by the request's maxHz — so it takes neither a truncation flag nor a cursor (§2.4 clause (d), pixel_attribution's `candidates` being the exemplar). THE UNIT IS UNSTATED by §6 (linear amplitude or dB): audit D-22.
