emulator/object_list.$comment: protocol.md §6 (object / player decoders), added 2026-08-26 by §11.25 (CR-D), closing audit D-27 for this row. A CLOSED ENVELOPE over an ENGINE-SHAPED payload: everything the contract owns is enumerated here, and the one part it cannot know - which named fields a given build's record has - is declared open as a typed map rather than left as a gap. §2.4's flat bounded-list spelling, as emulator/sprites uses it, with total/returned/limit/truncated as scalars beside the list. No cursor: the method accepts no continuation param, so a token it issued could never be handed back (§2.4 clause (b), lookup_symbol's ruling). A pure read: not subject to §6's run-control state rule, exactly as for read/sprites/pixel_attribution/scanlines - the envelope's `running` is the whole answer to a torn sample. One semantic divergence from sprites, deliberate: sprites pins total as {const:80} because every slot is an item there, while here an empty slot is NOT an item, so `total` counts ACTIVE objects and the table's size lives in layout.slotCount - two different facts, two homes.

limit.description: Max entries, from the lowest slot upward. Default: all active slots. Refused, never clamped, below 1 or above limits.maxObjectSlots (-32602).

fields.description: Layout field names to decode into each item's `fields` map. A name the layout does not have is -32602 with error.data.unknownFields carrying the offending names - §2.5's unknownParams shape one level down. The refusal precedes any decode, so a refused request has read nothing.

includeBytes.description: When true, each item carries `bytes`: its whole record verbatim. Off by default because 66 records at $50 is 5,280 bytes on every call for a caller who wanted two coordinates. Kept rather than deferred to emulator/read because the pool exceeds the catalogued read cap, so 'capture the whole pool' is at minimum two reads with no per-slot slicing and no layout stamp tying the bytes to the decode.

objects.description: ACTIVE slots only, ascending. Presence IS activity: an empty slot is omitted rather than returned with a flag that would always be true. Slot numbers are therefore sparse.

total.description: How many ACTIVE slots exist. NOT the table's size, which is layout.slotCount. total:0 beside truncated:false is 'zero objects' as a stated fact rather than an empty list a client must interpret.

limit.description: The ceiling actually applied, echoed so a caller can tell a default from its own request. May differ from the one asked for.

caveat.description: §2.4 rule 4: declared because this method CAN emit one, emitted CONDITIONALLY - when layout.detectedBy is 'fallback', or when the symbol table that produced the layout was accepted with binding:'indeterminate' (§4). Never on every reply: a caveat every reply carries is one nobody reads.

emulator/player_state.$comment: protocol.md §6 (object / player decoders), added 2026-08-26 by §11.25 (CR-D), closing audit D-27 for this row. object_list restricted to the player pool, with roles attached - the player is not a special record but an ordinary slot whose overlay window happens to be the player's. An ARRAY, never per-role keys: the legacy server's top-level key set VARIES BY ROM (player_1/player_2 on one branch, main/sidekick on the other, with an `engine` discriminant present on only one), which this repo's own transcription calls the biggest shape hazard in the eight; an array has a key set that does not vary, `role` carries the label without buying a key, and `layout` carries the discriminant on EVERY reply. No total/returned/truncated and no cursor: the player pool is structurally bounded, and §2.4 clause (d) says a structural bound takes neither. A pure read. NO DECODED BIT NAMES on any field: the legacy's names are invented, its two branches already disagree on the spelling of the same concept (in_air vs air, on_object vs onobject), §11.18 makes an emitted enum unwidenable, and a set-bits list carries strictly LESS than the raw value beside it because it cannot express a clear bit. A client asks for the raw field by name and applies the bit names it already has, from the source that defines them.

players.description: One entry per player SLOT, ascending - INACTIVE SLOTS INCLUDED, unlike object_list. 'Player 2 is not present' is the answer to the question asked, and a client must not have to infer it from an array's length against a bound it joins from elsewhere.

active.description: Whether this slot holds a live player. REQUIRED, false included: false is the answer, not the absence of one.

role.description: The server's label for this slot, from the layout - 'player', 'sidekick', ... A free string, for the reason layout.engine is one (§11.18). May be present on an inactive slot: the label is the slot's, not the occupant's.

caveat.description: As emulator/object_list.

emulator/object_at.$comment: protocol.md §11.26 (CR-F, ADOPT WITH CHANGES): one click, one answer, every failure named. A ⚙ decoder-group member (inherits -32012 and layout). Pure read, no require_paused. params are pixel_attribution's native-dot space with the same bounds.

x.description: Screen column, 0-based (D9 category 2 — a position a client counts with, not an address). Bounded here at the widest addressable value; the ACTIVE bound is the `width` this method reports, and a dot outside it is refused with -32004.

y.description: Screen line, 0-based. Same category and the same treatment as `x` — D9 names `line` among the JSON numbers, and this is that field.

emulator/object_slot.$comment: protocol.md §6 (object / player decoders), added 2026-08-26 by §11.25 (CR-D), closing audit D-27 for the third row of the family. The single-slot projection of emulator/object_list: the item keys hoisted to the top level, plus `active`, because this row ADDRESSES a slot and emptiness is therefore an answer rather than an omission. When active is false the reply is the slot facts and layout only - the decoded keys are omitted, never fabricated (§11.25, the M2 conditional on both rows that carry active). No consumer asked for it; it travels because leaving one row of a three-row family unschematized would leave the BLOCKED set meaning something its own reason does not say, and because a family with one absence convention is better than a family with two (the legacy emits '' for a missing name here and omits the key there). A slot past the pool is refused -32602 with the bound in error.data, on scanlines' precedent rather than pixel_attribution's -32004 - see §11.25, which records that the contract is split on this. NOTE the closure: this result declares NO additionalProperties, because a result top level composes replyFields and the closure that applies here is item 20's harness-side unevaluatedProperties, which sees through allOf.

slot.description: Index into the pool. Refused with -32602 at or above layout.slotCount, error.data carrying {slot, slotCount}: the fragment cannot bound it because the bound is a property of the loaded game.

active.description: Whether the addressed slot holds a live object. REQUIRED, false included: false is the answer, not the absence of one. When false, the decoded keys (x, y, code, name, nameDisp, fields, bytes) are FORBIDDEN - an empty slot's record is bytes the game never wrote, and reporting them would be the uninitialised-byte-as-datum shape rule (3) forbids for `fields`.

caveat.description: As emulator/object_list.

emulator/object_spawn.$comment: protocol.md §6 (object / player decoders ⚙), row at §6:1629; specified 2026-09-03 by §11.32 (CR-J, oracle 305b972, ADOPTED). The first of the family's three MUTATION rows, and a ⚙ group member: it inherits rule (1)'s REQUIRED `layout` and the -32012 a server with no symbol table owes instead of a decode from a guessed base, and it adds rule (5). Under rule (5) the server writes through a GAME-DEFINED MAILBOX whose cells it resolves BY NAME on every call — a build missing any required name is -32013 with error.data.missing naming every absent one, and is never written to at a computed address (§11.32 J5, the safety property: a release ROM cannot be written to at a guessed address) — and it owns the whole handshake (payload writes, the flag written last, the frame advance, the acknowledgement, the status read) as ONE INDIVISIBLE OPERATION ON THE ENGINE THREAD, so the client never sees a flag and no param here spells one (§11.32 J2). Named in §6's run-control state rule: a free-running machine is -32005 machineRunning, never an implicit pause. A REFUSAL BY THE GAME IS NEVER A RESULT FIELD (§8 item 25, §11.32 J3), which is why this fragment declares no `status`: the engine's non-zero codes leave as -32602 (a `def` that failed the archetype rails, error.data carrying `def` and naming all four rails because the engine's one status byte cannot say which), -32005 objectPoolFull (nothing was evicted), -32005 unknownSlot, -32005 slotOwnedByEntityWindow, and -32603 for an op byte the server itself wrote wrongly. `framesAdvanced` is REQUIRED on every reply, success and failure. THE RAW PLACEMENT WORD IS DELIBERATELY NOT A PARAM (§11.32 Q4): the engine masks it to $60FF silently, so a stray bit would be a value the caller set and the machine never saw — `subtype`/`flipH`/`flipV` are composed server-side instead, which is also what lets an out-of-range subtype be -32602 rather than a truncation. UNMEASURED and carried openly from the ruling: the frame counts (Q3), that layout.pools resolves on the build in question, and that the engine loop is single-request.

def.description: Address of the ObjDef archetype record to spawn from. D9 category 1. Exactly one of `def` and `defSymbol`, enforced by the oneOf above in BOTH directions (both present matches two branches, neither matches none) — emulator/write_memory's addr|symbol precedent, with the spellings NOT borrowed: §11.32 Q5 rules that `addr` on a spawn row reads as where to put it, which is `x`/`y`. A `def` outside the cart window is -32602 BEFORE any write is attempted.

defSymbol.description: The archetype named rather than addressed, resolved per call (D7). The ergonomic path: a client finds archetypes with emulator/lookup_symbol's bounded prefix search and hands the name straight back, which is why §11.32 adds no archetype-catalogue row. Typed as symbolName rather than as a bare non-empty string for the reason every symbol-typed param on this bus is: the name must ROUND-TRIP, and a trailing +$hex displacement is a number duplicated inside a string (§4). This row declares no `disp`, so there is nothing for such a suffix to mean here.

x.description: World PIXELS, not the engine's fixed-point word (D9 category 2, the decodedSlot convention). Bounded by the engine's own 16-bit position cell; out of range is -32602, refused and never clamped. ALSO bounded by the LOADED ACT (section 11.35, oracle CR-L, 2026-09-04): the valid box is [0, Level_Width) x [0, Level_Height), both resolved by name per call; outside it the server MUST refuse -32602 before any write, with error.data.reason one of outsideAct (outside a known extent), actExtentUnknown (the listing cannot answer; the server says it cannot check rather than treating the act as infinite), noActLoaded (both symbols read 0, the absence of an act). A schema cannot witness this refusal; it is a section 8 conformance obligation. Player_Bound_Right/_Bottom are NOT the act bounds (inset player clamp edges; objects are unclamped and a placement between them and Level_Width is legal and renders).

subtype.description: The archetype's subtype byte, composed into the placement word's low byte server-side. Bounded at a byte so an over-large value is -32602 rather than the engine's silent truncation.

flipH.description: Horizontal flip, composed into the placement word server-side.

flipV.description: Vertical flip, composed into the placement word server-side.

maxFrames.description: How many frames the server may advance the paused machine while waiting for the engine to acknowledge the request. A request unacknowledged within it is -32005 mailboxNotConsumed — never a success — and the server CANCELS it, clearing the request flag so it cannot fire minutes after its own error reply, and reporting error.data.cancelled true (§11.32 Q2). The default of 2 stands PROVISIONALLY: §11.32 Q3 leaves the frame counts unmeasured and says so. NO CEILING IS DECLARED because the contract states none; the run-shaped rows bound theirs by limits.maxRunFrames and this row is not yet tied to that limit.

expectFrameToken.description: Optional guard against acting on a machine that moved under the caller: compared against the current stamp, and a mismatch is -32005 frameMoved. Typed exactly as the `frameToken` this bus already carries (D9 category 2, the emulated frame index, minimum 0, NOT a handle) — a negative value could match no stamp this envelope can carry.

handle.description: The spawned object's handle: the LOW WORD of this record's `addr` (§11.32's re-read correction to CR-J §2.4 — object_list does not already report a handle field; it reports `addr`, of which this is the low word). A hex string under D9 category 1 and deliberately NOT #/$defs/handle's opaque token, because the contract states an arithmetic relationship between it and `addr`, and an opaque handle is one a client MUST NOT do arithmetic on.

addr.description: Bus address of the object's record — the full SST address, D9 category 1. P1: the key that makes the reply checkable with emulator/read and joinable to emulator/object_slot.

slot.description: Pool index, the join back to emulator/object_list. PRESENT IFF `layout` resolves it, never fabricated — the ⚙ group's rule (3) one level up. The server inverts the layout's slot addressing so the client never does address arithmetic; where the layout cannot supply it the key is omitted.

x.description: World pixels (D9 category 2), AS READ FROM THE OBJECT'S RECORD AFTER `framesAdvanced` FRAMES — never an echo of the accepted request (§11.32 addendum, 2026-09-03, oracle's ruling: an echo carries zero information, the client just sent those numbers; the re-read is the actual state of the machine, which is what every other reply on this bus reports). The moment is named because an unqualified position after a frame advance is a plausible wrong answer: these rows write POSITION ONLY and leave velocity untouched, so an object with velocity has moved by the time the acknowledgement is collected, and `framesAdvanced` on the same reply is what lets a client reason about how much time passed. STATED LIMIT, v1: the re-read conflates the engine adjusting a requested position on spawn with the object moving under its own velocity; `framesAdvanced` says time passed and does not separate the causes. Not a spawn-position confirmation. If a consumer ever needs the split it is an ADDED field (the accepted position), never a redefinition of this one. UNBOUNDED because a re-read after motion is not confined to the request's 0-65535.

y.description: See x: a re-read after `framesAdvanced` frames, not an echo, with the same stated limit.

framesAdvanced.description: How many frames the machine advanced to collect the engine's acknowledgement. REQUIRED on every reply, success and failure alike (rule (5)); on a failure it rides in error.data. 0 is a legal answer and IS the answer, not the absence of one. The machine is paused before and paused after: the advance is a change of POSITION, not of mode (§11.32 J4), which is why it is reported rather than treated as a mode change the caller must detect.

layout.description: What the server decoded against, and how — the ⚙ group's rule (1), which binds these rows exactly as it binds the read rows.

caveat.description: §2.4 rule 4, DECLARED here because §11.32 permits it on these rows and §11.20 permits a caveat only where the schema declares it. Emitted for exactly ONE thing: the residual window between the server's write and the engine's consumer when the machine was paused mid-frame, and only where the server can tell that it applied. A server that cannot tell emits none — an unconditional caveat on every reply is a field nobody reads. §11.32 Q3 leaves a hard -32005 pausedMidFrame open as an additive refusal once the window is measured.

emulator/object_move.$comment: protocol.md §6 (object / player decoders ⚙), row at §6:1630; specified 2026-09-03 by §11.32 (CR-J). emulator/object_spawn's rule (5) applies unchanged — mailbox cells resolved by name per call, one indivisible engine-thread operation, framesAdvanced on every reply, the game's refusals as typed errors — and only the addressing differs: `handle`|`slot`, the existing either-spelling convention (emulator/read, write_memory, memory_hash) applied to the same problem, since `slot` is what object_list reports and `handle` is what a previous object_spawn returned. TWO BEHAVIOURAL FACTS A CLIENT WILL ASSUME THE OPPOSITE OF, both normative and both stated here because they are the row's whole semantics: POSITION ONLY — velocity, status, angle and animation are untouched, so a moved badnik keeps doing what it was doing — and NO CLAMP, an out-of-act object is simply culled. A handle the pool does not hold is -32005 unknownSlot, the unknownCheckpoint/unknownBreakpoint precedent verbatim; where layout.pools resolves, a slot outside the dynamic pool is refused PRE-FLIGHT with -32602 naming that this row reaches the dynamic pool only, which fires only where the engine would have refused anyway (§11.32's 'Not proposed and not added' paragraph), and where pools does not resolve the engine's own refusal stands. Unlike delete, MOVE is allowed on a slot the entity window owns.

handle.description: The object's handle, as emulator/object_spawn returned it: the low word of the record's addr. D9 category 1. Exactly one of `handle` and `slot`, enforced in both directions by the oneOf above; both or neither is -32602.

slot.description: Pool index, as emulator/object_list reports it. Alternative to `handle`. A slot past the pool is -32602 with the bound in error.data, on the ⚙ group's rule (4).

x.description: New position, world PIXELS. As emulator/object_spawn for UNITS AND SPACE (pixels, D9 category 2, the 16-bit cell bound refused -32602) and NOT for the act bound: section 11.35's outside-the-act refusal applies to spawn only; this row's NO CLAMP fact in its $comment wins here, a move outside the act is a real, reversible state change to an addressable object and is accepted (corrected 2026-09-04 after 11.35 gave the misreading a citation; oracle's finding).

handle.description: As emulator/object_spawn — echoed whichever spelling the caller used, so a caller that addressed by `slot` still gets the handle.

slot.description: As emulator/object_spawn: present iff the layout resolves it, never fabricated.

x.description: As emulator/object_spawn: world pixels RE-READ from the record after `framesAdvanced` frames, never an echo of the accepted request (§11.32 addendum, 2026-09-03). The re-read matters more here than on spawn: this row moves an object that may already have velocity, so the value the caller sent is not where the object is.

caveat.description: As emulator/object_spawn.

emulator/object_delete.$comment: protocol.md §6 (object / player decoders ⚙), row at §6:1631; specified 2026-09-03 by §11.32 (CR-J). emulator/object_move's addressing and emulator/object_spawn's rule (5), with the position params dropped: a delete names a thing, not a place. NO `deleted: true` IN THE RESULT — a field that is true on every success is §11.5's 'released's defect with a useful name', and the failure path is a typed error, so the boolean could never carry information. Two behavioural facts, both normative: the delete CASCADES, taking the child chain with it, and a slot the entity window owns is refused -32005 slotOwnedByEntityWindow — the asymmetry with move, which is allowed on such a slot; the message must name the fix rather than reading as a malformed-request refusal, since the slot despawns on its own. Three rows and not one object_request{op} because servedness on this bus is `methods` membership (§8 item 23) and one row would make 'can spawn' and 'can delete' the same bit (§11.32 J1). capabilities.objectDecoders is true iff at least one of the three appears in `methods`, and never reports whether a layout was detected.

handle.description: As emulator/object_move. The handle of the record that was deleted; it names what the call acted on, which is the only thing left to report once the record is gone.

slot.description: As emulator/object_spawn: present iff the layout resolves it, never fabricated.

caveat.description: As emulator/object_spawn.

emulator/screen_text.$comment: protocol.md §6 (window text) and §11.29 (CR-H, oracle d907fae, ADOPT WITH CHANGES). Reads the text a human can read on the PLAYER window: status line, toasts, palette/lens readouts, the window-manager title bar. Serves the SOURCE string and the RENDERED prefix both, because rendered-only reports a message's shadow and source-only is structurally blind to truncation. A pure read of a snapshot the frontend already composed for drawing (pushed once per present); never composes on demand, touches no Vdp or System, sits outside state_hash. REFUSES with -32005 and error.data.reason 'noDisplay' when no window exists: an empty list is FORBIDDEN because 'a window showing no text' is the default launch state and already means something else. NO number inside any text corresponds to a bus field: the status line's F is a UI counter, not the machine's frame (F-WINDOW-BUS-FRAME-OFFBYONE, diagnosed 2026-08-30). SCHEMATIZED AHEAD OF BEING SERVED: vectors are owed by oracle, derived from a real reply and run against this fragment before the method is advertised.

result.$comment: §2.4's FLAT spelling of the bounded-list rule, as checkpoint_list uses: the list is the whole result. `surfaces` is bounded by what the player draws (a policy bound: toasts can stack), so it is cursor-less but carries total/returned/truncated so a client can never mistake a partial page for the screen.

total.description: Surfaces on the glass in total.

kind.description: Which surface. `titleBar` is drawn by the window manager, not the overlay, which is why the method is not named overlay_*.

text.description: The SOURCE string the player composed.

rendered.description: What is actually on the glass after the player's fit/truncation; a prefix of `text` today. Compare to `text` for the honest reading; `truncated` is a convenience, not the guard.

truncated.description: rendered != text. Derived; REQUIRED even when false.

unrenderable.description: Characters in `text` for which the player has no glyph (it draws a hollow box). Empty array when none; REQUIRED so absence and 'none' are not the same artifact. Measured 2026-08-30: backtick and em dash have no glyph and the player's own first toast contains a backtick.
